definition_zh: 灰白的；苍白的；像灰烬的；死灰色的
definition_en: pale gray in color, especially the gray-white of a shocked or frightened face
core_image: 听到噩耗后一瞬间血色尽失的脸
scene: 电话那头传来坏消息，她扶住桌沿，脸色瞬间褪成一片灰白。 Her face turned ashen when she read the telegram.
sceneCN: 这里 ashen 是「灰白的、死灰色的」（第 1 个义项：形容惊恐后的脸色）；句意是她读电报时脸色变得灰白。

derivatives.zh: 复合形容词，义为「面色灰白的」
由 ash 加后缀构成，义为「灰的；覆灰的」

senses.title: Pale from shock or fear
senses.definition: pale and gray, describing a face drained by fear or illness
senses.definitionCN: 苍白带灰，形容被恐惧或疾病抽干血色的脸
senses.example: The witness went ashen as he described the crash.
senses.exampleCN: 目击者描述事故时脸色变得死灰。
senses.why: Ash, the cold gray powder of burned wood, gives its color to a face emptied of blood.
senses.whyCN: 灰烬是木头燃尽后的冷灰色粉末，把这种颜色给了失去血色的脸。

senses.title: Gray like ashes
senses.definition: of a gray color like wood ash
senses.definitionCN: 像木灰一样的灰色
senses.example: After the wildfire, an ashen haze covered the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 山火过后，灰蒙蒙的烟霭笼罩山谷。
senses.why: The color comparison extends from faces to skies and landscapes.
senses.whyCN: 颜色比喻从脸色扩展到天空与景色。

intro.en: Ashen is ash plus the Old English adjectival suffix -en, meaning made of or like.
intro.cn: ashen 由 ash（灰烬）加古英语形容词后缀 -en（由…制成／像…）构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *askon meant burnt remains.
items.cn: 重构词根 *askon 指燃烧后的残余。

items.en: Asce meant ash, the powder left after burning.
items.cn: 古英语 asce 指灰烬。

items.en: The suffix -en made adjectives of material, as in wooden and golden.
items.cn: 后缀 -en 构成材质形容词，如 wooden、golden。

items.en: Middle English aschen first meant made of ash, then ash-colored.
items.cn: 中古英语 aschen 先指灰烬制的，后指灰色的。

items.en: Modern English favors the pale-face sense.
items.cn: 现代英语更常用「脸色灰白」义。

note.en: Ashen is stronger than pale: it carries the gray of ashes and a hint of dread.
note.cn: ashen 比 pale 更强：带有灰烬的灰色与一丝不祥。

entries.definition: having a pale gray face
entries.definitionCN: 面色灰白的

entries.definition: the gray powder left by fire; also a tree
entries.definitionCN: 灰烬；白蜡树

entries.definition: covered with or like ash
entries.definitionCN: 覆灰的；灰色的

entries.definition: of the pale gray of ashes
entries.definitionCN: 灰烬灰色的

entries.definition: similar ending but different root entirely
entries.definitionCN: 湾状构造（拼写后缀相似，词源不同）

entries.definition: light in color, lacking blood
entries.definitionCN: 苍白的

entries.definition: unhealthy pale
entries.definitionCN: 病态的苍白

entries.definition: sickly pale and weak-looking
entries.definitionCN: 憔悴苍白的

entries.definition: of the color between black and white
entries.definitionCN: 灰色的

entries.definition: deathly pale with terror
entries.definitionCN: 惨白的；可怕的

normalIntro.en: See ash + -en: a face the color of a cold fireplace.
normalIntro.cn: 记住 ash + -en：一张冷灰如熄灭壁炉的脸。

normal.en: -en makes material adjectives: wooden, golden, ashen.
normal.cn: -en 构成材质形容词：wooden、golden、ashen。

normal.en: the shock sense drains blood to leave ash color.
normal.cn: 惊吓抽走血色，留下灰烬之色。

normal.en: compare pallid and wan for other pale words.
normal.cn: 比较 pallid、wan 等其他「苍白」词。

normal.en: an ashen sky mirrors the dying fire.
normal.cn: 铅灰的天空映着将熄的火。

normal.en: ash the tree and ash the powder are different words.
normal.cn: 白蜡树与灰烬是两个不同的同形词。

abstract.en: Picture a fireplace the morning after: cold and gray.
abstract.cn: 想象壁炉过后的清晨：冰冷灰暗。

abstract.en: Feel the blood draining downward like ash settling.
abstract.cn: 感觉血色像落灰一样沉降下去。

abstract.en: See a landscape wrapped in a gray burial veil.
abstract.cn: 想象被灰色裹尸布罩住的风景。

examples.en: He turned ashen at the news of the accident.
examples.cn: 听到事故消息，他的脸变得灰白。

examples.en: An ashen dawn rose over the burned hills.
examples.cn: 灰蒙蒙的黎明在烧焦的山丘上降临。

examples.en: Her ashen lips could barely speak.
examples.cn: 她惨白的嘴唇几乎说不出话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿申」——阿（苦）得申不出话，脸都灰了，正如 ashen 的死灰色。

root: ash（古英语 asce，灰烬）+ -en（古英语材质形容词后缀），义为「像灰烬的、灰白的」。

sensesIntro.en: The gray of burnt wood colors first faces in shock, then skies and land after fire.
sensesIntro.cn: 烧尽木头的灰色先给受惊的脸着色，再给火灾后的天空与大地着色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face the color of cold ashes
core.cn: 核心意象：一张冷灰如烬的脸

branches.en: pallor of fear or illness
branches.cn: 恐惧或病中的苍白

branches.en: the gray of ashes on things
branches.cn: 事物的灰烬色

branches.en: the coldness of the color
branches.cn: 颜色自带的冷意

branches.en: scenes of ruin after fire
branches.cn: 火灾后的残破景象

branches.en: a face emptied of blood
branches.cn: 血色尽失的脸

intro.en: The Old English -en suffix still builds material adjectives in modern English.
intro.cn: 古英语后缀 -en 至今仍用于构成材质形容词。

latinIntro.en: Ash is a native Germanic word, so there are no Latin cognates.
latinIntro.cn: ash 是日耳曼本族词，没有拉丁同源词。

definition_zh: 旋转；自转；轮换；轮作
definition_en: the act of turning about an axis, one complete turn, or a regular succession in which people or crops take turns
core_image: 磨盘绕中间的轴不停转动，轴心不动，谷粒从孔里落下被碾开
scene: 磨坊里，石磨绕中间的轴转，谷物从孔里落进去，被磨成粉从边缘出来。 The rotation of the millstone crushed the grain in a single pass.
sceneCN: 这里指「绕轴转动的运动」（第 1 个义项：物体绕自身或外部轴心旋转）；句意为磨盘的转动一趟就把谷物碾碎。图中可辨识物件：石磨、中轴、谷粒、出粉口。

pos.zh: 旋转；自转；一次转动；轮换；轮作

senses.title: Turning about an axis
senses.definition: the movement of a body turning around a fixed axis
senses.definitionCN: 物体绕固定轴转动的运动
senses.example: The rotation of the millstone crushed the grain in a single pass.
senses.exampleCN: 磨盘的转动一趟就把谷物碾碎。
senses.why: rotatio in Latin named a turning, from rotare 'to turn' and rota 'wheel', so the noun begins as pure motion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 rotatio 指「转动」，来自 rotare「转」与 rota「轮」，因此这个名词最初就是纯运动。

senses.title: One complete turn
senses.definition: a single complete turn through three hundred and sixty degrees
senses.definitionCN: 转满三百六十度的一整圈
senses.example: The handle needs one full rotation to open the valve.
senses.exampleCN: 手柄需要转一整圈才能打开阀门。
senses.why: counting turns turned the process noun into a countable unit of angle.
senses.whyCN: 数圈数的需要，把过程名词变成了可计数的角度单位。

senses.title: Taking turns in order
senses.definition: a regular order in which people or groups take their turn
senses.definitionCN: 人或群体按固定次序轮流承担
senses.example: The doctors work in rotation so that someone is always awake.
senses.exampleCN: 医生们轮流值班，以保证总有人醒着。
senses.why: people succeeding one another in a fixed order trace a circle, so the turning image became a scheduling word.
senses.whyCN: 人按固定次序接替，轨迹像一个圆，于是转动的意象成了排班用词。

senses.title: Crop rotation
senses.definition: the practice of growing different crops in a fixed sequence on the same land
senses.definitionCN: 在同一块地上按固定顺序种不同作物的做法
senses.example: Crop rotation kept the soil from wearing out.
senses.exampleCN: 轮作使土壤不致耗尽。
senses.why: fields take their turn in a cycle, so agriculture borrowed the same circular scheduling idea.
senses.whyCN: 田地按周期轮流，农业借用了同一套循环排程观念。

senses.title: The spin of a celestial body
senses.definition: the turning of a planet, star or moon about its own axis
senses.definitionCN: 行星、恒星或卫星绕自身轴的转动
senses.example: The rotation of the earth makes the stars appear to move.
senses.exampleCN: 地球的自转使恒星看起来在移动。
senses.why: astronomy applied the general motion noun to the spin of whole worlds.
senses.whyCN: 天文学把这个泛运动名词用于整个世界的自转。

senses.title: A rotation in mathematics
senses.definition: a transformation that turns a figure about a fixed point by a given angle
senses.definitionCN: 把图形绕定点转过给定角度的变换
senses.example: A rotation of ninety degrees maps the square onto itself.
senses.exampleCN: 旋转九十度把这个正方形映到自身。
senses.why: geometry isolated the pure turn from the turning body and made it an operation.
senses.whyCN: 几何把纯粹的「转」从转动的物体中抽离出来，使之成为一种运算。

senses.title: Job or shift rotation
senses.definition: a system in which workers change duties or shifts on a fixed schedule
senses.definitionCN: 工人按固定时间表更换职责或班次的制度
senses.example: Shift rotation gave everyone a share of the night work.
senses.exampleCN: 班次轮换让每个人都分担夜班。
senses.why: the scheduling sense became an administrative term for fair distribution of work.
senses.whyCN: 排班义成了公平分配工作的管理术语。

senses.title: Figurative cyclical succession
senses.definition: a borrowed use for the regular return of seasons, fashions or generations
senses.definitionCN: 借指季节、风尚或世代的有规律回归
senses.example: The rotation of fashion brought the old coat back again.
senses.exampleCN: 时尚的循环让那件旧外套又回来了。
senses.why: anything that returns in order looks like a wheel turning, so the word serves cycles of every kind.
senses.whyCN: 任何按序回归之物都像轮子在转，因此这个词适用于各种循环。

intro.en: Rotation comes from Latin rotatio 'a turning', from rotare 'to turn', from rota 'wheel'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: rotation 来自拉丁 rotatio「转动」，来自 rotare「转」，再来自 rota「轮」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Rota meant 'wheel'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the link sometimes suggested to a root meaning 'to run or roll' is a reconstruction.
items.cn: rota 意为「轮」。其更深来源不确定；有人提出与意为「跑、滚」的词根有联系，那属重构。

items.en: Rotare meant 'to turn, revolve, rotate', used of wheels, bodies and cycles of time.
items.cn: rotare 意为「转、旋转、回旋」，用于轮子、天体与时间循环。

items.en: Rotatio, rotationis named the act of turning and supplied the English noun.
items.cn: rotatio, rotationis 指转动的动作，提供了英语名词。

items.en: The noun entered English in the sixteenth century, first in astronomy and mechanics.
items.cn: 这个名词在十六世纪进入英语，最初用于天文学与力学。

items.en: Crop rotation spread in the eighteenth century, extending the word from motion to scheduling.
items.cn: 轮作在十八世纪推广，把这个词从运动扩展到排程。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): rota has no established Indo-European ancestor, and the root often printed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：rota 没有已确定的印欧祖先，常为它印出的词根属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the look-alike nouns and adjectives from the same stem; group two holds near-meaning motion words.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干的形近名词与形容词；第二组是语义相近的运动词。

entries.definition: Relating to rotation; the adjective describes a property, while rotation is the motion.
entries.definitionCN: 与旋转有关的；形容词描述性质，而 rotation 是运动。

entries.definition: To turn about an axis or to take turns; it names the action, not the cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 绕轴转动或轮流；它指动作，而非周期。

entries.definition: The part of a machine that turns; it is a component, not the motion.
entries.definitionCN: 机器中转动的部件；是零件，而非运动。

entries.definition: Describing a machine that works by turning, such as a rotary engine.
entries.definitionCN: 描述靠转动工作的机器，如转子发动机。

entries.definition: One complete turn or one orbit around another body; rotation is spin about one's own axis.
entries.definitionCN: 完整的一转，或绕另一天体的公转；rotation 是绕自身轴的自转。

entries.definition: Rapid turning, often with the idea of speed or dizziness; rotation is neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 快速转动，常带速度或眩晕之意；rotation 是中性的。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for one movement around a point or for a place in a sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 绕一点转一次，或序列中一个位置的日常词。

entries.definition: A series that returns to its starting state; rotation stresses the turning motion inside a cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 回到起始状态的序列；rotation 强调循环中的转动。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin pieces and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁成分与真实固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: rota 'wheel' gives rotare 'to turn' and rotatio 'a turning'.
normal.cn: rota「轮」给出 rotare「转」与 rotatio「转动」。

normal.en: The family runs rotate, rotation, rotational, rotor, rotary.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 rotate、rotation、rotational、rotor、rotary。

normal.en: Earth's rotation is spin; its revolution is orbit.
normal.cn: 地球的 rotation 是自转；revolution 是公转。

normal.en: Crop rotation and job rotation both schedule turns.
normal.cn: 轮作与岗位轮换都在安排轮次。

normal.en: In rotation means taking turns in a fixed order.
normal.cn: 固定短语「轮流地」表示按固定次序轮班。

abstract.en: Picture a millstone turning while its centre stays still.
abstract.cn: 想象磨盘转动，中心却不动。

abstract.en: Picture a wheel of seasons returning to the same mark.
abstract.cn: 想象季节之轮回到同一个刻度。

abstract.en: Picture a rota where each name moves one place forward.
abstract.cn: 想象一张轮值表，每个名字向前挪一位。

examples.en: One rotation of the wheel lifts the bucket to the top.
examples.cn: 轮子转一圈就把桶提到顶。

examples.en: The rotation of the staff keeps night shifts fair.
examples.cn: 员工轮换使夜班分配公平。

examples.en: Crop rotation restored nitrogen to the field.
examples.cn: 轮作把氮归还给田地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rot（轮、转）+ ation（动作）」——轮子转起来这一动作 → 旋转、轮换

root: 拉丁 rota「轮」→ rotare「转」→ rotatio「转动」；rota 更深来源不确定，常为其提出的「跑、滚」词根属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one turn: a body about its axis, one full circle, people taking turns, fields taking turns, a planet spinning, a figure mapped onto itself, a shift schedule and any returning cycle.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一次转动：物体绕轴、一整圈、人轮流、田轮作、行星自转、图形映到自身、班次轮换，以及任何回归的循环。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a millstone turning around a fixed axle while the grain is crushed beneath it.
core.cn: 核心意象：磨盘绕固定轴转动，谷物在下面被碾碎。

branches.en: PURE TURN: physical motion and its mathematical abstraction.
branches.cn: 纯粹的转：物理运动及其数学抽象。

branches.en: COUNTED SPIN: one turn of a handle or of a world.
branches.cn: 可数的自转：手柄的一圈，或一个世界的一圈。

branches.en: SCHEDULED TURNS: people and shifts succeed one another.
branches.cn: 排定的轮次：人与班次彼此接替。

branches.en: FIELDS: crops return in a fixed order.
branches.cn: 田地：作物按固定次序回归。

branches.en: CYCLES: seasons, fashions and generations come round again.
branches.cn: 循环：季节、风尚与世代再次转回。

intro.en: Rotation is a Latin action noun from a noun of a wheel, so the whole family turns on one root.
intro.cn: rotation 是由「轮」的名词派生的拉丁动作名词，整个词族围绕一个词根转动。

latinIntro.en: Rota, rotare and rotatio supply rotation, rotate, rotor and rotary; -atio marks the action.
latinIntro.cn: rota、rotare 与 rotatio 提供 rotation、rotate、rotor 与 rotary；-atio 标记动作。

items.example: Rota is the root of the family.
items.exampleCN: rota 是这个词族的词根。
这个后缀构成动作名词。

items.example: Rotational speed is measured in radians.
The rotor spins inside the coil.
A rotary engine has no pistons.
The rotator holds the sample steady.

definition_zh: n. 商业化（英式拼写，美式 commercialization）
definition_en: the process of making something into a business or selling it for profit
core_image: 老码头被改成商铺，招牌一路排开
scene: 这座老码头被改造成商铺，引来对过度商业化的批评。 The old dock became shops, and critics blamed its commercialisation.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：commercialisation 指商业化；句意是这座老码头被改造成商铺，引来对过度商业化的批评。

senses.title: The process of turning into business
senses.definition: the process of making an activity into a business that earns money
senses.definitionCN: 把某项活动变成盈利事业的过程
senses.example: The commercialisation of the festival changed its mood.
senses.exampleCN: 节日的商业化改变了它的气氛。
senses.why: Latin commercium is trade, and -isation names a process.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 commercium 意为贸易，-isation 表示过程。

senses.title: Excessive focus on profit
senses.definition: the disapproving sense of putting money before value
senses.definitionCN: 带有批评意味，指把金钱置于价值之上
senses.example: Critics fear the commercialisation of education.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者担心教育的过度商业化。
senses.why: The negative tone grew in twentieth-century debate.
senses.whyCN: 这一贬义语气在二十世纪争论中形成。

intro.en: Commercialisation is commerce plus a modern process suffix.
intro.cn: commercialisation 是 commerce 加上现代表示「过程」的后缀。

items.en: Com means together.
items.cn: com 意为一起。

items.en: Mercari means to trade.
items.cn: mercari 意为贸易。

items.en: Commercium means trade.
items.cn: commercium 意为贸易。

items.en: Commerce names the world of trade.
items.cn: 十六世纪 commerce 指贸易世界。

items.en: Commercial describes trade matters.
items.cn: 十九世纪 commercial 形容贸易事务。

items.en: Commercialisation names the process.
items.cn: 二十世纪 commercialisation 指这一过程。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the commerc- shape; the near-meaning group names market processes.
note.cn: 形近组共享 commerc- 词形；近义组列出市场化的说法。

entries.definition: Relating to trade.
entries.definitionCN: 商业的。

entries.definition: Excessive emphasis on profit.
entries.definitionCN: 商业主义。

entries.definition: To make into a business.
entries.definitionCN: 使商业化。

entries.definition: Making something a market.
entries.definitionCN: 市场化。

entries.definition: Moving into private hands.
entries.definitionCN: 私有化。

entries.definition: Turning into a corporation.
entries.definitionCN: 公司化。

normalIntro.en: Commercialisation adds a process ending to the word for trade.
normalIntro.cn: commercialisation 在「贸易」一词后加上表示过程的后缀。

normal.en: Mercari means to trade.
normal.cn: mercari 意为贸易。

normal.en: Commerce is the world of trade.
normal.cn: commerce 是贸易世界。

normal.en: Commercial means of trade.
normal.cn: commercial 意为商业的。

normal.en: -isation means a process.
normal.cn: -isation 表示过程。

normal.en: Commercialisation turns things into business.
normal.cn: commercialisation 把事物变成生意。

abstract.en: Shop signs on an old pier.
abstract.cn: 旧码头上的一排店招。

abstract.en: A price tag on a hobby.
abstract.cn: 爱好上的价签。

abstract.en: A song turned into an advert.
abstract.cn: 被改成广告的歌曲。

examples.en: The commercialisation of the sport worries fans.
examples.cn: 这项运动的商业化让球迷担忧。

examples.en: Rapid commercialisation changed the town.
examples.cn: 快速商业化改变了这座小镇。

examples.en: They protested against the commercialisation of art.
examples.cn: 他们抗议艺术的商业化。

dict_mnemonic.text: commercial（商业的）+ -isation（过程）→ 使变得商业化，即商业化。

root: 拉丁 com（一起）+ mercari（贸易）→ commercium → commerce → commercial → commercialisation

sensesIntro.en: The neutral process of becoming business, and the negative worry about it.

definition_zh: 分期付款；一期；一集；部分
definition_en: one of several regular payments for a debt; one part of a series
core_image: 一本日历，每个月都被划掉一个方格，方格上标着小小的金额数字
scene: 小丽想买一台最新款的电脑，商店说可以分十期付，每期两百块。 She decided the installment plan was easier than paying all at once.
sceneCN: 这里 installment 指「分期付款的一期」（第 1 个义项：债务的定期分期付款之一）；句意为他们选择分月付而不是一次性付清。图中可辨识物件：日历、电脑、分期付款收据。

pos.zh: 分期付款（可数）；一集（可数）

senses.title: regular debt payment
senses.definition: one of a series of scheduled payments to settle a debt
senses.definitionCN: 结清债务的一系列预定付款之一
senses.example: The loan required twelve monthly instalments.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔贷款要求分十二个月偿还。
senses.why: The root is install, 'to set up', as in setting up a schedule of payments.
senses.whyCN: 词根是 install「设立」，就像设立一个付款日程。

senses.title: part of a purchase
senses.definition: one part of the price of an item paid over time
senses.definitionCN: 一件商品的价格中按时间分批支付的一部分
senses.example: They bought the fridge on easy instalments.
senses.exampleCN: 他们以轻松分期的方式买下了冰箱。
senses.why: A purchase that you set up with a payment plan.
senses.whyCN: 通过付款计划设立的一笔消费。

senses.title: episode of a story
senses.definition: one episode of a serial story, television show or podcast
senses.definitionCN: 连载故事、电视剧或播客的一集
senses.example: The novel was published in monthly instalments.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说按月连载。
senses.why: A story set up to come out piece by piece.
senses.whyCN: 被设立成一段一段推出的故事。

senses.title: stage of a plan
senses.definition: one stage of an overall plan or project
senses.definitionCN: 整体计划或项目的一个阶段
senses.example: The first instalment of the highway opened in 2024.
senses.exampleCN: 高速公路的一期在 2024 年通车。
senses.why: A large work set up as a series of smaller bits.
senses.whyCN: 一项大工程被设立成若干小块。

senses.title: artwork installation
senses.definition: a large artwork set up in a specific space
senses.definitionCN: 设立在特定空间里的大型艺术作品
senses.example: The museum commissioned a new instalment.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆委托创作了一件新的装置作品。
senses.why: A work that is installed, set up in a space.
senses.whyCN: 一件被 install、设立在空间里的作品。

senses.title: initial payment
senses.definition: the first payment in a series
senses.definitionCN: 一系列付款中的第一笔
senses.example: The first instalment was due on delivery.
senses.exampleCN: 首期款在交货时到期。
senses.why: The first of the scheduled pieces.
senses.whyCN: 预定的几块中的第一块。

senses.title: supplement or tranche
senses.definition: a supplementary sum of money released over time
senses.definitionCN: 随时间分批释放的一笔追加资金
senses.example: The donor promised a second instalment in 2026.
senses.exampleCN: 捐赠者承诺 2026 年捐出第二期款项。
senses.why: Money set up to come in slices.
senses.whyCN: 被设立成一片片进来的钱。

senses.title: scheduled meeting
senses.definition: a scheduled session of a course or training programme
senses.definitionCN: 课程或培训项目预定的一节课
senses.example: The leadership course had six fortnightly instalments.
senses.exampleCN: 这个领导力课程分六次，每两周一次。
senses.why: A course set up as pieces over time.
senses.whyCN: 一门被设立成若干块、按时间推出的课程。

intro.en: Instalment comes from install 'to set up, arrange' + -ment. Install itself came from Old French installer, from Latin installare.
intro.cn: instalment 来自 install「设立、安排」+ -ment。install 本身来自古法语 installer，后者来自拉丁语 installare。

items.en: Latin installare meant 'to place in a seat, to install in an office'; it was in- 'in' + stallum 'seat, stall'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 installare 意为「安置在座位上、任命」，由 in-「在……里」+ stallum「座位、栏」构成。

items.en: Old French installer meant 'to install, establish'.
items.cn: 古法语 installer 意为「安装、设立」。

items.en: English install was borrowed around 1400 meaning 'to place formally, to establish'.
items.cn: 英语 install 约 1400 年从古法语借入，意为「正式安置、设立」。

items.en: Instalment was formed from install + -ment around 1560, first meaning 'an arrangement, a setting up'.
items.cn: instalment 约 1560 年由 install + -ment 构成，最初意为「一个安排、一次设立」。

items.en: The 'partial payment' sense developed from the idea of 'setting up a debt to be paid in parts', by the 18th century.
items.cn: 「分期付款」义来自「设立一笔要分几块还的债」的想法，18 世纪形成。

items.en: Installment (US) and instalment (UK) are both standard; the Latin root stallum is well attested.
items.cn: 美式 installment 和英式 instalment 都是标准拼写；拉丁词根 stallum 来源可靠。

note.en: Look-alikes share the install root; near meanings are one of several payments or parts.
note.cn: 形近共享 install 词根；近义是若干付款或部分中的一个。

definition_zh: 排水；排水系统；排出的水；流域；引流
definition_en: the system or process by which water is removed from land, soil or a wound
core_image: 一片积水的田里，几条暗沟把水引向低处的河，水面一寸寸退下去
scene: 暴雨过后，低洼的农田积起半尺深的水，田垄间几条暗沟正把浑水引向旁边的河。 Faulty drainage left the lower fields under water for a week.
sceneCN: 这里 drainage 指「排水系统、排水设施」（第 1 个义项：把地表或土壤中的水引走的沟渠与管网）；句意为排水系统出了故障，低处的田地积水达一周之久。

pos.zh: 排水；排水系统；排出的水；（医学）引流

senses.title: The system that carries water away
senses.titleCN: 排水系统：把水引走的整套设施
senses.definition: the network of ditches, pipes and channels that removes water from an area
senses.definitionCN: 把水从某地引走的沟渠、管道与渠道系统
senses.example: Faulty drainage left the lower fields under water for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 排水系统出了故障，低处的田地积水达一周之久。
senses.why: drainage is drain plus -age, and -age names a process or the whole apparatus that carries it out; the village owns not one ditch but a connected set of them.
senses.whyCN: drainage 是 drain 加 -age，而 -age 表示过程或执行该过程的整套装置；村子拥有的不是一条沟，而是一组相连的沟渠。

senses.title: The act of draining water off
senses.titleCN: 排水过程：把水排走这件事
senses.definition: the process of removing surplus water from soil, land or a structure
senses.definitionCN: 把多余的水从土壤、土地或建筑物中排走的过程
senses.example: Good drainage keeps the clay soil workable after heavy rain.
senses.exampleCN: 排水良好能让黏土在暴雨后仍然可耕。
senses.why: the same suffix names the action itself, so the word can refer to what is done rather than to the works that do it.
senses.whyCN: 同一个后缀也命名动作本身，因此这个词可以指「排水这件事」，而不是干这件事的设施。

senses.title: Water that has been drained away
senses.titleCN: 排出的水：被引走的液体
senses.definition: the water, often waste water, that is carried off by drains
senses.definitionCN: 被排水设施引走的水，常指污水
senses.example: The drainage from the mine carried heavy metals into the stream.
senses.exampleCN: 矿井排出的水把重金属带进了小溪。
senses.why: by metonymy the container word comes to name its contents: what the drains carry is also called drainage.
senses.whyCN: 通过转喻，容器之名转而指其中的内容：排水设施所输送的水也被叫作 drainage。

senses.title: The land area that sends water to a river
senses.titleCN: 流域：把水汇给某条河的地面
senses.definition: the whole area whose surface water flows into a particular river or basin
senses.definitionCN: 地表水全部流入某条河或某个盆地的整个区域
senses.example: The drainage of the upper valley feeds three reservoirs.
senses.exampleCN: 上谷的集水区供养着三座水库。
senses.why: hydrologists speak of what a river drains, so drainage shifts from the channel to the land that supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 水文学家谈「一条河排走哪片地面的水」，于是 drainage 从河道转到供养它的土地。

senses.title: How readily soil lets water through
senses.titleCN: 土壤排水性：水通过的快慢
senses.definition: the rate at which water moves down through soil or rock
senses.definitionCN: 水在土壤或岩层中向下移动的速率
senses.example: Heavy clay has poor drainage and stays wet for days.
senses.exampleCN: 重黏土的排水性差，会连续几天保持潮湿。
senses.why: a soil is judged by how fast it drains, so the abstract noun names a property of the ground rather than a structure.
senses.whyCN: 人们用「水排得多快」来评价土壤，因此这个抽象名词指的是地面的一种性质，而非某种结构。

senses.title: Medical drainage of a wound
senses.titleCN: 医学引流：把伤口液体引走
senses.definition: the removal of fluid from a wound or body cavity, or the fluid so removed
senses.definitionCN: 把液体从伤口或体腔引出，或指这样引出的液体
senses.example: The nurse checked the drainage from the wound each morning.
senses.exampleCN: 护士每天早上检查伤口的引流液。
senses.why: medicine applies the same image to the body: fluid is given a path out, and the word names both the procedure and its product.
senses.whyCN: 医学把同一意象用到身体上：给液体一条出路，这个词既指操作也指引出的东西。

senses.title: Pumping water out of a mine or tunnel
senses.definition: the removal of ground water from a mine, tunnel or construction pit
senses.definitionCN: 从矿井、隧道或施工基坑中抽走地下水
senses.example: Mine drainage must be pumped out before the shaft can be deepened.
senses.exampleCN: 在加深竖井之前，必须先把矿井积水抽走。
senses.why: the engineering sense narrows the general idea to water that must be lifted out of a hole, because gravity will not do the work.
senses.whyCN: 工程义把一般概念收窄为「必须从坑里提上来的水」，因为重力无法把它带走。

senses.title: A steady loss of people or resources
senses.titleCN: 资源与人力的持续外流
senses.definition: a continuing loss of people, money or resources from a place or system
senses.definitionCN: 人、资金或资源从一个地方或系统中持续流失
senses.example: The drainage of trained nurses to big cities weakened the rural clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 受训护士流向大城市，削弱了乡村诊所。
senses.why: the metaphor treats a community as ground that loses its water through channels, leaving it dry.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把社区当作会沿沟渠失水的地面，水流走之后只剩干涸。

intro.en: Drainage is the native verb drain plus the noun suffix -age. Drain goes back to Old English dreahnian 'to strain out, draw off liquid', and -age reached English through Old French from Latin -aticum. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: drainage 是英语本族动词 drain 加名词后缀 -age 构成。drain 上承古英语 dreahnian「沥出、滤干液体」；-age 经古法语来自拉丁 -aticum。年代均为约数。

items.en: Dreahnian meant to strain or draw off liquid, and was used of a wound, a vessel or wet ground. The modern verb drain shortened both the vowel and the ending.
items.cn: dreahnian 意为沥出、引流液体，用于伤口、容器或潮湿地面。现代动词 drain 缩短了元音与词尾。

items.en: By the fourteenth century drainen is recorded for emptying a pond or a ditch. The noun drain, meaning a channel, appears later, in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 到 14 世纪，drainen 已用于排空池塘或沟渠。表示通道的名词 drain 出现较晚，在 16 世纪。

items.en: The suffix -age entered English with Old French, from Latin -aticum, which formed nouns of action or collective status; attached to a verb it names the process or the set of works.
items.cn: 后缀 -age 随古法语进入英语，源自拉丁 -aticum，用来构成动作或集合状态的名词；接在动词后即命名过程或整套设施。

items.en: The noun drainage is recorded in the seventeenth century in writing on fen reclamation and water meadow management.
items.cn: 名词 drainage 在 17 世纪见于沼泽开垦与草甸灌溉管理的文献。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the word covers urban sewerage, mine dewatering and the drainage basin as a unit of land.
items.cn: 19 世纪，这个词覆盖城市排污、矿井排水以及作为土地单元的流域。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of drain is not settled; a link with Old English drygan 'to dry' is often proposed but not demonstrated, and the first dates above are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根存疑）：drain 的更深来源没有定论；把它与古英语 drygan「使干」相联系的说法常被提出，但未获证实；上述首见年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds water-handling words that are constantly swapped; group two holds the terms for the land area that feeds a river.
note.cn: 第一组是常被互换的水利词汇；第二组是命名「供养一条河的地面」的术语。

entries.definition: A single pipe or ditch that carries water away; drainage is the whole arrangement of such channels.
entries.definitionCN: 单条把水引走的管或沟；drainage 则是这类通道的整套安排。

entries.definition: An underground conduit built for sewage; drainage may also carry clean rain water.
entries.definitionCN: 专为污水建的地下管道；排水系统也可能输送干净的雨水。

entries.definition: Water that flows over the surface instead of entering the soil; drainage is what removes it.
entries.definitionCN: 未渗入土壤而在地表流走的水；排水系统负责把它引走。

entries.definition: Bringing water to land on purpose; drainage takes water away from it.
entries.definitionCN: 有意把水送到土地上；排水则把水从土地上带走。

entries.definition: The area from which rain and streams feed one river or reservoir.
entries.definitionCN: 雨水与小河汇入同一条河或同一水库的区域。

entries.definition: Either the dividing ridge between basins or, in North American usage, the basin itself.
entries.definitionCN: 既可指流域之间的分水岭，也可在北美用法中指流域本身。

entries.definition: A river, stream or artificial channel through which water flows.
entries.definitionCN: 水流经的河、溪或人工渠道。

entries.definition: The point or amount at which water leaves a lake, basin or system.
entries.definitionCN: 水离开湖泊、盆地或系统的出口或数量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real compounds and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的后缀、复合词与固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: drain + -age: the -age noun names what the verb does, as in seepage and leakage.
normal.cn: drain + -age：-age 名词命名动词所做的事，如 seepage、leakage。

normal.en: A drainage basin is not a basin you wash in: it is the land that drains into one river.
normal.cn: drainage basin 不是洗脸的盆，而是把水排入同一条河的土地。

normal.en: The word covers both the ditches and the water in them, as printing can mean the act and the product.
normal.cn: 这个词既指沟渠也指沟里的水，正如 printing 既可指印刷行为也可指印刷品。

normal.en: Medical drainage uses the same picture: fluid is shown a way out of the body.
normal.cn: 医学引流用同一幅画面：给液体一条离开身体的出路。

normal.en: Poor drainage is a soil property; blocked drainage is a broken system. The context tells you which reading is meant.
normal.cn: poor drainage 说的是土壤性质，blocked drainage 说的是系统堵塞；上下文决定读法。

abstract.en: A city without drainage is a city that keeps every storm it has ever met.
abstract.cn: 没有排水系统的城市，会把遇到过的每一场暴雨都留在原地。

abstract.en: When talented people leave a region, economists borrow the word and call it a drainage of talent.
abstract.cn: 人才离开某地时，经济学家借用这个词，称之为人才的流失。

abstract.en: A good conversation has drainage too: small channels that let pressure out before it floods.
abstract.cn: 好的对话也有排水：细小的通道让压力在泛滥之前先泄出去。

examples.en: The new drainage system carries rainwater away from the market.
examples.cn: 新的排水系统把雨水从市场引走。

examples.en: Poor drainage turns the path into mud after every storm.
examples.cn: 排水不良使小路每场暴雨后都变成泥浆。

examples.en: Engineers mapped the drainage of the whole valley before building the dam.
examples.cn: 工程师在筑坝前测绘了整个山谷的集水区。

dict_mnemonic.text: drain（排走）+ -age（过程、集合）＝把水引走的整套安排；沟渠、管网、流域都归到「水往哪里走」这一条线。

root: 由动词 drain（排走液体）加后缀 -age（过程、集合）构成；drain 上承古英语 dreahnian「沥出、滤干」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of drainage. The core is a path given to water: first the works, then the act, then the water itself, then the land that supplies it, and finally any steady outflow.
sensesIntro.cn: drainage 的八个义项。核心是「给水一条路」：先是设施，再是动作，再是被引走的水，再是供养它的土地，最后是任何持续的外流。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water is given a path and led away from where it is not wanted.
core.cn: 核心意象：给水一条路，把它从不需要它的地方引走。

branches.en: WORKS AND ACT: the connected channels, then the process they perform.
branches.cn: 设施与动作：先是相连的通道，再是它们执行的过程。

branches.en: WHAT MOVES AND WHERE FROM: the water carried off, then the land that supplies it.
branches.cn: 流动之物与来源：先是被引走的水，再是供养它的土地。

branches.en: A PROPERTY OF GROUND: how fast soil lets water pass, with no pipe in sight.
branches.cn: 地面的性质：土壤让水通过得多快，此时并不需要管道。

branches.en: REMOVAL BY FORCE OR BY DESIGN: fluid drawn from a wound, water pumped from a mine.
branches.cn: 借力或设计而成的排出：从伤口引出液体，从矿井抽水。

branches.en: OUTFLOW AS LOSS: people and money leaving a place are treated as water leaving dry land.
branches.cn: 外流即流失：人与钱离开某地，被当作水离开干地。

intro.en: Drainage is drain plus -age. The suffix, not the root, is the borrowed element: -age turns the verb into the name of a process and of the apparatus that performs it.
intro.cn: drainage 由 drain 加 -age 构成。借来的是后缀而非词根：-age 把动词变成过程之名，也变成执行该过程的装置之名。

latinIntro.en: Drain itself is a Germanic word with no Latin cognate. Only the suffix is Latin in origin, coming through French from -aticum; Latin ripa and the drain family are unrelated.
latinIntro.cn: drain 本身是日耳曼语词，没有拉丁同族词。只有后缀源自拉丁，经法语来自 -aticum；拉丁 ripa 与 drain 词族无关。

items.example: The farmer drained the field before sowing.
items.exampleCN: 农夫在播种前把田里的水排干。

items.meaning: process, state or a collective set
items.example: Drainage, seepage and leakage all name processes.

items.meaning: a channel or pipe that carries liquid away
items.example: A drain runs along the edge of the road.

items.meaning: a device or person that drains
items.example: She lifted the drainer out of the sink.
items.exampleCN: 她把沥水架从水槽里拿起来。

items.example: He felt drained after the long shift.
items.exampleCN: 长时间值班后他感到精疲力竭。

items.meaning: the act of removing liquid; exhausting
items.example: Draining the pond took two days.

items.meaning: the land area drained by one river system
items.meaningCN: 由同一河系排水的陆地区域
items.example: The city lies inside the drainage basin of the Yangtze.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市位于长江流域之内。

items.meaning: a pipe that carries waste water away
items.example: A broken drainpipe flooded the basement.
items.exampleCN: 一根破损的排水管淹了地下室。

definition_zh: 装饰品；装饰物；装饰纹样；为场所增光的人或物；装饰音；仪式礼器；装饰、点缀（动词）
definition_en: a small object or added detail that decorates something; a person or thing that brings distinction; a musical flourish; a set of ceremonial vessels; also a verb meaning to adorn
core_image: 一只玻璃小球挂上圣诞树最低的枝条，整棵树因为这一点亮光就显出了节日的样子
scene: 圣诞树已经立好在客厅角落，彩球和细链正一层层挂上去， She lifts a glass ornament from the box and hooks it onto a low branch.
sceneCN: 这里 ornament 指「悬挂起来的小件装饰物」（第 1 个义项：单件装饰品）；句意为她从盒子里取出一只玻璃挂饰，挂到较低的枝条上。图中可辨识物件：立好的圣诞树、装挂饰的纸盒、玻璃球与细链。

derivatives.zh: 装饰；装饰品；整体装饰体系

senses.title: A small object kept for display
senses.titleCN: 为陈列而保留的小件装饰物
senses.definition: a small object, often hanging or standing, that is kept and shown because it makes a place look better
senses.definitionCN: 常为悬挂或摆放的小件物品，因能让场所更好看而被保留、陈列
senses.example: A single silver ornament hung at the centre of the tree.
senses.exampleCN: 树的中央挂着一件银质小饰品。
senses.why: This is the concrete end of the word: Latin ornamentum named the fittings of a house or a person, and English narrowed that set down to one pretty object.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最具体的一端：拉丁 ornamentum 本指房屋或人的配备之物，英语把这一整组收窄成单独一件好看的物件。

senses.title: An added detail on a made object
senses.titleCN: 制成品表面上的附加纹样
senses.definition: a pattern, carving or inlay added to an object to make it more beautiful rather than more useful
senses.definitionCN: 为让物件更美而不是更有用而添加的图案、雕刻或镶嵌
senses.example: The brass clock is covered in engraved ornament.
senses.exampleCN: 这座黄铜钟上布满雕刻纹饰。
senses.why: Once the object itself is no longer the unit, the word can name any added surface detail, and the emphasis moves from the thing to the marking.
senses.whyCN: 当计量单位不再是物件本身，这个词就能指任何附加的表面细部，重心也从物件转到纹样。

senses.title: Decoration built into a building
senses.definition: a decorative feature of a building, such as a moulding, capital or carved panel, that is part of the structure
senses.definitionCN: 建筑上的装饰性构件，如线脚、柱头或雕刻板，本身属于结构的一部分
senses.example: The porch is enriched with stone ornament in a leaf pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 门廊以叶片纹样的石雕装饰增色。
senses.why: Architecture needed a word for decoration that is fixed in place, and ornament supplied it because the Latin noun already meant the fittings of a structure.
senses.whyCN: 建筑需要一个指固定不动的装饰的词，本词正好合用，因为拉丁名词本就是指建筑的配备件。

senses.title: A person who graces a group
senses.definition: a person whose presence or achievements bring credit to a place, profession or occasion
senses.definitionCN: 其在场或成就为某地、某行业或某场合带来荣誉的人
senses.example: The retired judge was an ornament to the small committee.
senses.exampleCN: 这位退休法官是那个小委员会的一大光彩。
senses.why: The figurative step treats social value as visible beauty: someone who makes a group look better is, in the old sense, a fitting.
senses.whyCN: 这一步比喻把社会价值当作可见的美：让群体显得更体面的人，按旧义就是一件合宜的配备之物。

senses.title: Adornment itself, not the thing
senses.definition: the quality or act of adorning, considered apart from any single object
senses.definitionCN: 脱离任何单件物品来看的装饰性质或装饰行为
senses.example: The carving was added for ornament, not for strength.
senses.exampleCN: 这道雕刻是为装饰而加，并非为了加固。
senses.why: English allows the noun to be a mass noun, so the word can name adornment in general and stand opposite to use or function.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许这个名词作不可数用法，于是它能泛指装饰，并与用途、功能相对。

senses.title: An added note that beautifies a line
senses.titleCN: 为旋律增色的附加音符
senses.definition: a grace note, trill or turn added to a melody to make it more elaborate
senses.definitionCN: 为使旋律更繁复而加入的倚音、颤音或回音
senses.example: The pianist added a small ornament at the end of each phrase.
senses.exampleCN: 钢琴家在每一乐句的结尾加了一个小装饰音。
senses.why: Music borrowed the idea directly: what is added for beauty rather than necessity is an ornament, and the term survived as a technical label.
senses.whyCN: 音乐直接借用了这一想法：为美而非为必需添加的东西就是装饰，这个说法作为术语沿用下来。

senses.title: Vessels and fittings of a ceremony
senses.titleCN: 仪式所用的器皿与陈设
senses.definition: the decorated vessels and furnishings used in a religious or state ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 宗教或国家仪式上使用的装饰性器皿与陈设
senses.example: The cathedral keeps its silver ornament locked in the treasury.
senses.exampleCN: 主教座堂把银质礼器锁在宝物室里。
senses.why: Here the older collective sense returns: ornament is not one pretty thing but the whole set of fittings proper to a solemn place.
senses.whyCN: 这里回归较古老的集合义：本词不是一件好看的东西，而是一个庄严场所应有的整套陈设。

senses.title: To decorate something (verb)
senses.definition: to decorate or embellish something, especially in a careful or formal way
senses.definitionCN: 装饰或点缀某物，尤指用心地、正式地加以修饰
senses.example: Fresh laurel ornamented the doorway for the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 为这场典礼，新鲜的月桂装饰了门廊。
senses.why: The verb keeps the Latin verb's active sense of fitting something out, and its stress falls on the last syllable, which sets it apart from the noun.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了拉丁动词「为某物配齐装备」的主动义；重音落在末音节，与名词区分开来。

intro.en: Ornament comes from Latin ornamentum 'equipment, adornment', a noun built on the verb ornare 'to equip, fit out, adorn'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ornament 来自拉丁语 ornamentum「装备、装饰物」，由动词 ornare「装饰、配备」加名词后缀 -mentum 构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ornare meant 'to equip, fit out, adorn'. It was used of preparing a person, a house or a ship for use, so adornment and equipment were the same act.
items.cn: ornare 意为「装备、配备、装饰」。它用于把人、房屋或船准备停当，所以装饰与配备在当时是同一个动作。

items.en: The suffix -mentum formed nouns of means or result, so ornamentum was the equipment or furnishing of something, and by extension its adornment.
items.cn: 后缀 -mentum 构成表示手段或结果的名词，因此 ornamentum 指某物的装备与陈设，进而指它的装饰。

items.en: Old French took the noun as ornement and kept both faces of it, the furnishing of a place and the beauty added to it.
items.cn: 古法语接受这个名词并把它变作自己的形式，两面都保留下来：场所的陈设，以及为之增添的美。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the thirteenth century; early uses covered church furnishing, military equipment and adornment generally.
items.cn: 英语在 13 世纪借入这个词；早期用法涵盖教堂陈设、军备以及一般意义上的装饰。

items.en: Later the noun narrowed to a single decorative object, and a verb ornament 'to adorn' grew beside it, with the stress moved to the final syllable.
items.cn: 后来名词收窄为单件装饰物，旁边又长出动词 ornament「装饰」，重音移到末音节。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin source of ornare is not established, so any Indo-European root proposed for it is a reconstruction rather than a witnessed form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：ornare 在拉丁语之前的来源并无定论，凡为其提出的印欧词根均属重构形式，而非实际书证。

note.en: The first group holds words that look or sound close to ornament, including one from another root; the second holds near synonyms that differ in whether they name an object, an act or a whole scheme.
note.cn: 第一组是与本词形近或音近的词，其中有一个来自别的词根；第二组是近义词，区别在于所指是一件物品、一个动作还是一整套方案。

entries.definition: Elaborately decorated; it goes back to the same Latin verb ornare, but it describes a style rather than an object.
entries.definitionCN: 装饰繁复的；同出拉丁动词 ornare，但描述的是风格而非物件。

entries.definition: Serving as decoration; formed from this noun with an adjective suffix, so it answers the question of what a thing is for.
entries.definitionCN: 作装饰用的；由本词加形容词后缀构成，回答的是「它作何用」。

entries.definition: Military supplies and guns; it comes from the same source as the word for a decree, not from ornare.
entries.definitionCN: 军械与火炮；与表示「法令」的词同源，与 ornare 无关。

entries.definition: The act or result of decorating, and a neutral cover term for anything added for beauty; it belongs to the decorare family, not the ornare family.
entries.definitionCN: 装饰的行为或结果，也是任何为美观而添加之物的中性统称；属 decorare 一族，与 ornare 一族不同源。

entries.definition: The act of adorning or the thing added; it comes from adorn, which is Latin adornare, ornare with the prefix ad-.
entries.definitionCN: 装饰的行为或添加之物；来自表示「装饰」的英语动词，其拉丁语形式由「装饰」词根加表示「向」的前缀构成。

entries.definition: A detail added to make something richer or more interesting, often in speech or writing as well as in design.
entries.definitionCN: 为使事物更丰富或更有趣而添加的细节，既用于设计与写作，也用于言谈。

entries.definition: A small ornament of little value; it names the object and implies cheapness, which this word does not.
entries.definitionCN: 价值不高的小饰物；指物件并含廉价之意，而本词不含此意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin pieces, the real word family and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁构件、真实的同族词，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: Ornare 'to equip' plus -mentum 'means or result' gives the fittings of a thing, and later its finery.
normal.cn: ornare「配备」加 -mentum「手段或结果」= 一件东西的配备，后来成了它的华饰。

normal.en: A ship's ornamenta were once its gear; the word still carries that old idea of fitting something out.
normal.cn: 船的 ornamenta 原本指它的索具装备；这个词至今仍带着「为某物配齐」的旧意。

normal.en: The noun puts the stress at the front and the verb puts it at the end; the shift marks the change of job.
normal.cn: 名词把重音放在前面，动词把重音放在末尾；重音的移动标记了词性的转换。

normal.en: Architects call a fixed decorative feature an ornament, never a decoration, because it is built into the fabric.
normal.cn: 建筑师把砌进本体的固定饰件称作装饰细部，而不说「装饰」，因为它属于结构本身。

normal.en: Christmas ornaments are small, many and hung, so the plural suits objects that arrive in sets.
normal.cn: 圣诞挂饰小而多、逐件悬挂，复数形式正适合成批出现的物件。

abstract.en: Picture one bright bead on a dark tree: the whole room changes because a small thing was added.
abstract.cn: 想象暗色圣诞树上的一颗亮珠：只因添了一件小东西，整个房间都变了。

abstract.en: Picture a plain doorway that becomes ceremonial the moment laurel is tied across it.
abstract.cn: 想象一道普通的门，在系上一条月桂的那一刻变得庄重。

abstract.en: Picture a person who is of no use in the room but makes the room worth entering.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人，在房间里并无用处，却让这房间值得走进去。

examples.en: She keeps a box of glass ornaments for the tree.
examples.cn: 她留着一盒玻璃挂饰，专供圣诞树用。

examples.en: The lintel carries a carved ornament of overlapping leaves.
examples.cn: 门楣上有一道叠叶纹样的雕刻装饰。

examples.en: Hosts ornament the table with branches and small candles.
examples.cn: 主人用枝条和小蜡烛装饰餐桌。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，那门」——门口挂的那串小饰物，就是装饰品。拉丁 ornare 是「配备、装饰」，配上去的多余之物，正是装饰。名词重音在前，动词重音在后，读音也跟着换了身份。

root: 拉丁 ornare「装饰、配备」加名词后缀 -mentum「手段或结果」构成 ornamentum「装备、装饰物」，经古法语进入英语；名词指装饰物，动词指装饰。ornare 在拉丁语之前的来源不确定，相关印欧词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from a single hanging object through surface detail, built ornament, a person who brings credit, adornment as such, a musical note and a set of ceremonial vessels, and end with the verb 'to adorn'.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从单件悬挂饰品出发，经过表面纹样、建筑饰件、为群体增光的人、装饰本身、音乐装饰音与仪式礼器，最后落在动词「装饰」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one small bright thing added to a plain surface, so that the whole surface reads as cared for.
core.cn: 核心意象：在素净的表面上添一件小而亮的东西，整个表面因此显得被用心对待。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the concrete end of the word, a piece kept because it makes a place look better.
branches.cn: 物件：这个词最具体的一端，一件因能让场所更好看而被保留的东西。

branches.en: SURFACE AND STRUCTURE: the same idea moves from a marking on an object to a feature built into a building.
branches.cn: 表面与结构：同一想法从物件上的纹样移到砌进建筑的构件。

branches.en: PERSON AND QUALITY: adornment can be a human presence that brings credit, or the abstract act of adorning itself.
branches.cn: 人与性质：装饰可以是为群体增光的在场之人，也可以是抽象的装饰行为本身。

branches.en: SPECIALISED SETS: music keeps the added-for-beauty idea in a single note, while ceremony keeps the older collective sense of fittings.
branches.cn: 专门领域：音乐把「为美而添加」收在一个音符上，仪式则保留较早的「整套陈设」集合义。

branches.en: THE VERB: the act of fitting something out with beauty, with the stress moved to the last syllable.
branches.cn: 动词：为某物配齐美观之物的动作，重音移到末音节。

intro.en: Ornament is built from one Latin verb, one Latin noun suffix and a small English family, so it can be read piece by piece.
intro.cn: ornament 由一个拉丁动词、一个拉丁名词后缀和一小族英语派生词构成，可以逐块读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin ornare 'to equip, adorn' gives ornamentum and the English family; the suffix -mentum marks means or result, and English later added -al and -ation for quality and process.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ornare「配备、装饰」衍生出 ornamentum 与英语这一族词；拉丁后缀 -mentum 表示手段或结果，英语后来又加表示性质与过程的后缀。

items.example: The verb describes the act of fitting something out.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描述为某物配齐装备的动作。

items.meaning: means or result of an action
items.example: The suffix turns the act of fitting out into the fittings themselves.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「配齐」的动作变成所配之物。

items.example: Latin used the noun for the fittings of a house, a ship or a person.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语用这个名词指房屋、船只或人的配备之物。

items.example: English kept both the noun and the later verb.
items.exampleCN: 英语同时保留了名词和后来出现的动词。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun into an adjective of function.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成表示用途的形容词。

definition_zh: n. 工艺品；美术器皿（统称，不可数）
definition_en: Decorative objects such as ceramics, glass and metal pieces considered together as a class of goods rather than as single works.
core_image: 货架上一排排只为好看而做的瓶瓶罐罐
scene: 橱窗里摆着一排青瓷花瓶与铜盘。 The window displayed Chinese artware in blue and bronze.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：artware 是工艺品的统称，把它当一类货品来看，而不是单件作品。

senses.title: Decorative objects as a class
senses.titleCN: 作为一类货品的装饰器物
senses.definition: ceramics, glass, metal and similar pieces made mainly to be looked at, spoken of together
senses.definitionCN: 主要为观赏而做的陶瓷、玻璃、金属等器物，作为一个整体来谈
senses.example: The museum shop sells local artware.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆商店出售本地工艺品。
senses.why: The second half, ware, means goods, so the word counts things by shelf rather than by masterpiece.
senses.whyCN: 后半 ware 意为「货品」，所以这个词是按货架而不是按杰作来数东西的。

senses.title: A trade category
senses.definition: the heading used in shops, catalogues and customs lists for decorative goods
senses.definitionCN: 商店、目录与报关清单上用来归类装饰性货品的名目
senses.example: Artware forms a separate line in the export list.
senses.exampleCN: 工艺品在出口清单上单列一项。
senses.why: Because the word names a class of goods, it fits invoices and catalogues where artwork would sound too grand.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词指的是一类货品，它适合发票与目录，而 artwork 在那里显得过于隆重。

intro.en: Artware joins art, from Latin ars, skill, to ware, from Old English waru, goods: skill turned into things for sale.
intro.cn: artware 由 art（源自拉丁语 ars「技艺」）与 ware（源自古英语 waru「货品」）拼成：技艺变成了可售的物件。

items.en: Latin ars meant skill or craft, the trained ability to make something well.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ars 意为「技艺、手艺」，即把东西做好的训练出来的能力。

items.en: Old French art carried the Latin sense of skill into the western languages.
items.cn: 古法语 art 把拉丁语「技艺」的意思带入西部各语言。

items.en: Old English waru meant goods or wares, the things a trader carries, and survives in hardware and silverware.
items.cn: 古英语 waru 意为「货品」，即商人携带之物，如今仍留在 hardware 与 silverware 中。

items.en: English ware came to name a whole class of made things, usually joined to the material or purpose.
items.cn: 英语 ware 转而指一整类制成品，通常与材料或用途拼合使用。

items.en: Nineteenth-century trade English joined the two halves to name decorative goods sold in quantity.
items.cn: 十九世纪的商贸英语把两半拼起来，指成批出售的装饰性货品。

items.en: Twentieth-century catalogues and customs lists kept artware as a heading beside ceramics and glassware.
items.cn: 二十世纪的目录与报关清单把 artware 与陶瓷、玻璃器皿并列，作为一个品类名目保留下来。

note.en: The look-alike group splits the two halves of the compound; the near-meaning group names the crafts that fill the shelf.
note.cn: 形近组把这个复合词的两半拆开来比；近义组列出填满货架的各类手艺名称。

entries.definition: A finished piece of art or an illustration.
entries.definitionCN: 一件完成的美术作品或插图。

entries.definition: Tools and metal goods, or computer parts.
entries.definitionCN: 工具与金属制品，或计算机硬件。

entries.definition: Pottery fired at a low temperature.
entries.definitionCN: 低温烧制的陶器。

entries.definition: Clever in a crafty, slightly sly way.
entries.definitionCN: 机灵而略带狡黠的。

entries.definition: Objects made from fired clay.
entries.definitionCN: 烧制黏土做成的器物。

entries.definition: Work made skilfully by hand.
entries.definitionCN: 用手精巧做出的活计。

entries.definition: Things produced by a skilled craft.
entries.definitionCN: 由熟练手艺做出的东西。

entries.definition: An object kept only for decoration.
entries.definitionCN: 纯为装饰而摆放的物件。

normalIntro.en: Artware is art plus ware, goods: skill on a shelf, priced by the piece rather than hung in a gallery.
normalIntro.cn: artware 就是 art 加 ware「货品」：摆在货架上的技艺，按件标价，而不是挂进美术馆。

normal.en: Ware always means a class of goods.
normal.cn: ware 一律表示一类货品。

normal.en: Hardware, silverware and glassware follow the same pattern.
normal.cn: hardware、silverware、glassware 都是同一构词法。

normal.en: Artware is uncountable, so use a piece of artware.
normal.cn: artware 不可数，要说 a piece of artware。

normal.en: Artwork is one piece, artware is the whole shelf.
normal.cn: artwork 是一件，artware 是整架。

normal.en: The word belongs to shops and catalogues.
normal.cn: 这个词属于商店与商品目录。

abstract.cn: 想象报关单上有一个「装饰货品」的格子。

abstract.en: Think of skill packed into a crate for shipping.
abstract.cn: 想象技艺被装箱待运。

examples.en: The stall was piled with painted artware.
examples.cn: 摊子上堆满彩绘工艺品。

examples.en: She buys artware whenever she travels.
examples.cn: 她每次旅行都会买工艺品。

examples.en: Artware and textiles fill the lower floor.
examples.cn: 工艺品与织物占满了下一层。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：art「艺术」+ ware「器皿、货品」——摆成货卖的艺术品，就是工艺品 artware。

root: 拉丁语 ars「技艺」经古法语 art 入英语；古英语 waru「货品」给出 ware；十九世纪商贸英语把两者拼成 artware，指成批出售的装饰器物。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses treat beauty as stock: objects made to be looked at, and the catalogue heading under which they are shipped and sold.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都把「美」当作库存：为观赏而做的器物，以及它们被运输与销售时所归入的目录名目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shelves of jars and vases made only to be looked at
core.cn: 核心意象：货架上一排排只为好看而做的瓶瓶罐罐

branches.en: Blue vases and bronze plates in a window.
branches.cn: 橱窗里的青花瓶与铜盘。

branches.en: A stall piled with painted pieces.
branches.cn: 堆满彩绘器物的摊子。

branches.en: One line on an export list.

branches.en: Beauty counted as stock, not as masterpieces.
branches.cn: 把美当库存来数，而不是当杰作。

intro.en: Artware is art plus -ware; the same goods ending builds hardware, glassware and silverware, while art adds -istic and -isan.
intro.cn: artware 是 art 加 -ware；同一「货品」后缀构成 hardware、glassware 与 silverware，而 art 一侧则派生出 -istic 与 -isan 一类形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is ars, skill, artifex, a skilled maker, and artificium, a crafted thing; the ware half stays Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 ars「技艺」、artifex「巧匠」与 artificium「手工制品」；ware 那一半仍是日耳曼来源。

latinEntries.example: Ars opens the whole art family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ars 是整个 art 词族的起点。

definition_zh: 勤勉的；刻苦的；一丝不苟的；殷勤备至的
definition_en: showing great care, attention, and persistent effort in work or duty
core_image: 清晨到深夜都不离开书桌的学生
scene: 图书馆闭馆的铃声响了，他仍在灯下逐行核对译稿，笔记本边缘已被手指磨得发亮。 The assiduous student revised every footnote before dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 assiduous 是「勤勉的、一丝不苟的」（第 1 个义项：对工作持续用心）；句意为这位勤奋的学生在黎明前核完了每条脚注。

derivatives.zh: 同根名词，义为「勤勉；殷勤」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「勤勉地」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「勤勉」

senses.title: Showing persistent care and effort
senses.definition: giving constant and careful effort to a task
senses.definitionCN: 对任务付出持续而细致的努力
senses.example: Her assiduous preparation won the debate.
senses.exampleCN: 她的刻苦备战赢得了辩论。
senses.why: Latin assiduus meant sitting beside the work, so the adjective describes one who never leaves the task.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 assiduus 意为「坐在工作旁」，形容词描绘寸步不离任务的人。

senses.title: Attentive and courteous to others
senses.definition: showing constant attentive service toward a person
senses.definitionCN: 对人表现出持续的细心侍奉
senses.example: The assiduous waiter refilled glasses before anyone asked.
senses.exampleCN: 殷勤的侍者不等人开口便续上了水。
senses.why: Staying seated beside a guest becomes staying close in service.
senses.whyCN: 「坐在宾客身旁不离」化作侍奉中的常伴左右。

intro.en: Assiduous comes from Latin assiduus, constant, literally sitting beside, from assidere.
intro.cn: assiduous 源自拉丁语 assiduus（持续的，字面为「坐在旁侧」），出自 assidere。

items.en: The root *sed- meant to sit.
items.cn: 词根 *sed- 意为坐。

items.en: Assidere meant to sit beside or attend to.
items.cn: 拉丁语 assidere 意为坐在旁侧、侍奉。

items.en: Assiduus described one who stays at the task without leaving.
items.cn: assiduus 形容坚守岗位不离的人。

items.en: English borrowed assiduous in the sixteenth century alongside assiduity.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语与 assiduity 一同借入 assiduous。

items.en: It now labels both tireless work and attentive care.
items.cn: 如今它既形容不倦的工作，也形容周到的照料。

note.en: Assiduous keeps the image of staying seated until the job is done.
note.cn: assiduous 保留了「坐定不动直到完工」的画面。

abstract.en: See one chair worn smooth by daily sitting.

abstract.en: Feel the hush of early morning study hours.
abstract.cn: 体会清晨自习时段的静谧。

examples.en: An assiduous editor caught every stray comma.
examples.cn: 一位一丝不苟的编辑抓住了每个多余的逗号。

examples.en: The assiduous nurse checked on him every hour.
examples.cn: 殷勤的护士每小时查看他一次。

examples.en: Assiduous practice made the pianist fluent.
examples.cn: 刻苦的练习让钢琴家琴艺纯熟。

sensesIntro.en: Staying seated at the task yields both tireless work and devoted care.
