senses.titleCN: 整体的舒适程度与基本生活保障
senses.definition: the general level of comfort in which people live, judged by food, housing, health care and other necessities
senses.definitionCN: 人们生活的一般舒适程度，以食物、住房、医疗等基本需要衡量
senses.example: The survey compares the standard of living of rural households with that of city dwellers.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查把农村家庭的生活水平与城市居民作比较。
senses.why: The phrase pairs a measuring rod with the act of living, so it asks how well, not merely whether, people live.
senses.whyCN: 这个词组把「衡量尺度」与「生活」放在一起，问的是人们过得好不好，而不只是有没有在活。

senses.title: Measured by goods and services per person
senses.titleCN: 按人均商品与服务衡量
senses.definition: the level of consumption of goods and services available to each person
senses.definitionCN: 每个人可以使用到的商品与服务数量所体现的水准
senses.example: A rising standard of living shows up as more varied food and better housing per person.
senses.exampleCN: 生活水平提高，会表现为人均食物更丰富、住房更好。
senses.why: Consumption is the most visible face of comfort, so a per-person basket of goods became the common measure.
senses.whyCN: 消费是舒适最直观的一面，因此人均商品篮成了常用尺度。

senses.title: A national or regional average
senses.titleCN: 国家或地区的平均水平
senses.definition: the average condition of a whole population rather than of one household
senses.definitionCN: 整群人口的平均状况，而非单个家庭的状况
senses.example: The standard of living in the capital is far above the national average.
senses.exampleCN: 首都的生活水平远高于全国平均。
senses.why: Once the phrase is applied to a population, it becomes an average that hides differences inside the group.
senses.whyCN: 这个词组一旦用于整群人口，就成了掩盖群体内部差异的平均值。

senses.title: A minimum acceptable threshold
senses.titleCN: 可接受的最低生活水准
senses.definition: the minimum level of comfort and provision that a society considers acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会认为可以接受的最低舒适与供给水平
senses.example: Charity workers argued that no family should fall below a basic standard of living.
senses.exampleCN: 慈善工作者主张，任何家庭都不应跌到基本生活水平以下。
senses.why: A measuring rod can mark a floor as well as an average, and the floor sense drives welfare policy.
senses.whyCN: 尺子既能标出平均线，也能标出底线，底线义推动了福利政策。

senses.title: Quality of life beyond material goods
senses.titleCN: 超出物质层面的生活质量
senses.definition: the part of wellbeing that comes from leisure, education, health and a clean environment rather than income alone
senses.definitionCN: 来自闲暇、教育、健康与清洁环境而非单纯收入的福祉部分
senses.example: Planners now include green space when they discuss the standard of living.
senses.exampleCN: 规划者在讨论生活水平时，如今把绿地也计算在内。
senses.why: Living well is not only owning much, so the phrase stretched to cover the non-material side of comfort.
senses.whyCN: 过得好不只是拥有得多，这个词组因此扩展到舒适的非物质层面。

senses.title: A level that rises over time
senses.titleCN: 随时间提高的生活水准
senses.definition: the historically changing level of comfort that each generation expects as normal
senses.definitionCN: 每一代人视为正常、并随历史变化的舒适程度
senses.example: Each generation measures the standard of living against what its parents already had.
senses.exampleCN: 每一代人都以父辈已经拥有的条件来衡量生活水平。
senses.why: Expectations are learned, so what counts as adequate shifts upward as goods become ordinary.
senses.whyCN: 期待是被养成的，商品一旦普及，所谓「够用」的标准就随之上移。

senses.title: Purchasing power against the cost of living
senses.titleCN: 与生活成本相对的购买力水平
senses.definition: the real level of comfort given a money income, after the prices people must pay are taken into account
senses.definitionCN: 在计入人们必须支付的价格之后，一定货币收入带来的实际舒适程度
senses.example: A pay rise that only matches prices leaves the standard of living unchanged.
senses.exampleCN: 只与物价涨幅持平的加薪，不会改变生活水平。
senses.why: Comfort depends on what money can buy, so the phrase is always read against prices rather than income alone.
senses.whyCN: 舒适取决于钱能买到什么，因此这个词组总要对照物价来读，而不能只看收入。

senses.title: Official statistical indicator
senses.definition: an index or set of indicators used by governments and agencies to report living conditions
senses.definitionCN: 政府与机构用来报告生活状况的指数或一组指标
senses.example: The annual report tracks the standard of living through housing, health and schooling indicators.
senses.exampleCN: 年度报告通过住房、健康与教育指标追踪生活水平。
senses.why: When comfort is reported as numbers, the phrase becomes the name of the indicator itself.
senses.whyCN: 当舒适被报成数字，这个词组便成了指标本身的名称。

intro.en: Standard has an uncertain Frankish origin and reached English through Old French; living is a native Germanic word. The full phrase is a modern social and statistical term. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 前半经古法语进入英语，可能来自法兰克语，来源不确定；后半是日耳曼语本族词。完整词组是近现代的社会与统计术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Standard goes back to Old French estandart 'banner, rallying point'. A common suggestion derives it from a Frankish form meaning 'stand firm', but that form is a reconstruction and the source is uncertain.
items.cn: 「标准」可追溯到古法语 estandart「旗帜、集合点」。常见假说认为它来自法兰克语中表示「站稳」的形式，但该形式属重构，来源不确定。

items.en: English adopted the word in the fourteenth century for a banner and then for an authorized weight or measure, from which the modern sense of a level of quality grew.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入该词，先指旗帜，后指官方认可的度量衡，现代「水准」义由此发展而来。

items.en: Living comes from Old English libban 'to live', a native Germanic verb with no Latin ancestor.
items.cn: 「生活」部分来自古英语表示「活着」的动词，是日耳曼语本族词，没有拉丁语祖先。

items.en: The full phrase appeared in the nineteenth century, when reformers needed a term for the material conditions of workers and the poor.
items.cn: 完整词组出现于十九世纪，当时改革者需要为工人与穷人的物质状况命名。

items.en: In the twentieth century the phrase became a statistical measure of consumption, housing and access to services.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个词组成为衡量消费、住房与服务可及性的统计指标。

items.en: Source uncertain (Frankish origin): no attested Frankish form survives, and the earliest use of the full phrase is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（法兰克语来源）：没有留存可证的法兰克语形式，完整词组的最早用例也没有确切年代。

note.en: Group one holds phrases that look almost identical but measure something else; group two holds words that describe how well people live.
note.cn: 第一组是外形几乎相同、却测量别的东西的词组；第二组是描述人们过得好不好的词。

entries.definition: The cost of living is the money needed to buy everyday goods and services; the standard of living is the comfort those purchases actually deliver.
entries.definitionCN: 生活成本是购买日常商品与服务所需的钱；生活水平则是这些购买实际带来的舒适程度。

entries.definition: Living standard is the common reversed form with the same meaning; standard of living is the more formal statistical phrasing.
entries.definitionCN: 生活水准是其常见的倒序形式，含义相同；生活水平是更正式、更统计化的说法。

entries.definition: Quality of life covers health, freedom, environment and happiness, while the standard of living leans on material provision.
entries.definitionCN: 生活质量涵盖健康、自由、环境与幸福感，生活水平则偏向物质供给。

entries.definition: A way of life is the customs and habits of a group, not a measurable level of comfort.
entries.definitionCN: 生活方式是一群人的习俗与习惯，不是可测量的舒适程度。

entries.definition: Wellbeing includes health, security and satisfaction, of which material comfort is only one part.
entries.definitionCN: 福祉包含健康、安全与满足感，物质舒适只是其中一部分。

entries.definition: Affluence is a high level of wealth and consumption; it describes the top end that the standard of living measures on average.
entries.definitionCN: 富裕是财富与消费的高水平，描述生活水平在均值上衡量的高端。

entries.definition: Prosperity is the success of an economy or group, a condition that usually raises the standard of living.
entries.definitionCN: 繁荣是经济或群体的成功状态，通常会抬高生活水平。

entries.definition: Material conditions are the concrete housing, food and services behind any standard of living.
entries.definitionCN: 物质条件是任何生活水平背后的住房、食物与服务等具体基础。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real halves, real measures and real phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词两半、真实的度量与真实的说法，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: A standard is a measuring rod; living is being alive; together they ask how well a life measures.
normal.cn: 标准是一把尺，生活是活着，合起来就是问日子量出来有多好。

normal.en: The phrase is reported as a number, but it always describes people's actual conditions.
normal.cn: 这个词组虽以数字报告，却始终描述人们的实际处境。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the floor sense: a basic standard of living, a decent standard of living.
normal.cn: 固定搭配体现底线义：基本生活水平、体面生活水平。

normal.en: It is read against prices, because money alone does not buy comfort.
normal.cn: 它要对照物价来读，因为单有钱并不等于舒适。

normal.en: It is close to cost of living, but the two point in opposite directions: one is comfort, the other is price.
normal.cn: 它与生活成本相近，但方向相反：一个说舒适，一个说价格。

abstract.en: Picture a table set with just enough plates, and then with more than enough.
abstract.cn: 想象一张餐桌先摆出刚好够用的盘子，后来又摆出用不完的盘子。

abstract.en: Picture a thermometer that measures not heat but how easily a family gets food and medicine.
abstract.cn: 想象一支温度计，量的不是热度，而是一家人获得食物与药品的容易程度。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder whose lowest rung is called decent and whose top is never reached.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子，最下一级叫「体面」，最高一级永远够不到。

examples.en: The report found a wide gap in the standard of living between the coast and the interior.
examples.cn: 报告发现沿海与内陆之间生活水平差距很大。

examples.en: Rising incomes do not automatically raise the standard of living when rents rise just as fast.
examples.cn: 当租金涨得同样快时，收入增加并不会自动提高生活水平。

examples.en: Clean water and schooling are now counted as part of the standard of living.
examples.cn: 清洁饮水与教育如今被计入生活水平。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「标准」加「生活」——用一把尺去量日子过得好不好，就是生活水平

root: 前半经古法语 estandart「旗帜、集合点」进入英语，可能来自法兰克语重构形式，来源不确定；后半为古英语本族词，意为「活着」。合起来指生活所达到的水准。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of measuring: a life is held against goods, against an average, against a floor, against prices and finally against a printed indicator.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个衡量动作展开：把生活分别对照商品、平均值、底线、物价，最后对照公布的指标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a family table, a roof and a medical bill placed side by side as one measuring rod.
core.cn: 核心意象：把餐桌、屋顶与医疗账单并排放好，合成一把衡量生活的尺。

branches.en: THE BASKET: comfort is first read off the goods and services a person can actually use.
branches.cn: 篮子：舒适首先从一个人实际能用的商品与服务读出来。

branches.en: THE AVERAGE: one basket is multiplied into a population figure.
branches.cn: 平均值：一只篮子被放大成整群人口的数字。

branches.en: THE FLOOR AND THE REPORT: a minimum is set, then published as an indicator.
branches.cn: 底线与报告：先设最低线，再作为指标公布。

branches.en: BEYOND GOODS: comfort extends to leisure, health and a clean environment.
branches.cn: 超出商品：舒适扩展到闲暇、健康与清洁环境。

branches.en: TIME AND PRICE: expectations rise, and money is always read against what it can buy.
branches.cn: 时间与价格：期待会上移，而钱总要对照它能买到什么来读。

intro.en: The phrase joins a word of uncertain Frankish origin for an authorized measure with a native Germanic word for being alive.
intro.cn: 这个词组把来源不确定、经古法语而来的「官方尺度」与日耳曼语本族的「活着」拼在一起。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here: the first half is Frankish through French, and the second half is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语来源：前半经法语来自法兰克语，后半是英语本族词。

items.example: The hotel fell below its own standard.
items.exampleCN: 这家旅馆没达到它自己的标准。

items.meaning: to make uniform by a standard
items.example: The agency standardized the forms across regions.
items.exampleCN: 该机构把各地表格统一标准化。

items.example: Standardization cut the cost of spare parts.
items.exampleCN: 标准化降低了备件成本。

items.meaning: the state or activity of being alive
items.example: The cost of living rose sharply.
Many families live on one income.
items.exampleCN: 许多家庭靠一份收入生活。

items.example: The city became more livable after the parks opened.
items.exampleCN: 公园开放后这座城市更宜居了。

items.example: Fishing remains the main livelihood here.
items.exampleCN: 捕鱼仍是这里的主要生计。

items.meaning: the measure of a life's comfort
items.example: The phrase names what the indicators try to capture.
items.exampleCN: 这个词组命名了各项指标试图捕捉的东西。

definition_zh: 爱情的；恋爱的；与性爱有关的
definition_en: relating to love, especially sexual love
core_image: 写着情诗的鹅毛笔：专为爱情而生的词
scene: 书房里诗人正在为心上人写下情诗。 He kept his amatory verses hidden in a locked drawer.
sceneCN: 这里的 amatory 是「爱情的」（第 1 个义项：与恋爱有关的）；句意是他把情诗藏在锁着的抽屉里。

derivatives.zh: 同族名词，义为「爱好者；业余爱好者」，源自同一拉丁词根
同族形容词，义为「多情的；含情脉脉的」
由 amor 加名词后缀构成，义为「写情爱题材的作家；多情的人」

senses.title: Relating to love or courtship
senses.titleCN: 爱情的：与恋爱求爱相关
senses.definition: connected with romantic love or the act of courtship
senses.definitionCN: 与浪漫爱情或求爱行为相关的
senses.example: The poet is famous for his amatory sonnets.
senses.exampleCN: 这位诗人以爱情十四行诗闻名。
senses.why: The Latin root amor means love, and the adjective simply marks anything devoted to it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根 amor 意为爱，形容词只是标记一切与爱情有关的事物。

senses.title: Expressing sexual desire
senses.definition: expressing or suggesting physical passion between lovers
senses.definitionCN: 表达或暗示恋人间的肉体情欲
senses.example: The novel contains several amatory scenes.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说里有几段情爱描写。
senses.why: Latin amor covered desire as well as affection, so the adjective keeps both colors.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 amor 兼指欲望与爱慕，这个形容词因此保留两层色彩。

senses.title: Characteristic of a lover
senses.titleCN: 恋人般的：具有恋人姿态的
senses.definition: having the manner or style typical of a lover courting someone
senses.definitionCN: 具有求爱者典型举止或风格的
senses.example: He gave her an amatory glance across the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他隔着桌子向她投去含情的一瞥。
senses.why: From describing love poetry, the word widened to describing loving behavior.
senses.whyCN: 从描述爱情诗扩展到描述示爱的行为举止。

senses.title: Relating to love affairs in literature
senses.definition: in literary criticism, describing works built on romantic plots
senses.definitionCN: 文学批评中形容以恋爱情节为主线的作品
senses.example: Amatory fiction flourished in eighteenth-century England.
senses.exampleCN: 言情小说在十八世纪的英国盛极一时。
senses.why: Critics needed a compact label for the love-plot genre, and the Latin adjective served.
senses.whyCN: 批评家需要一个简洁标签指称言情体裁，拉丁语形容词便派上用场。

senses.title: Devoted to the pursuit of love
senses.titleCN: 沉溺恋爱的：热衷求爱的
senses.definition: given to or occupied with romantic adventures
senses.definitionCN: 醉心于恋爱韵事或情感冒险的
senses.example: The hero leads an amatory life through half of Europe.
senses.exampleCN: 主人公在半个欧洲过着猎艳般的风流生活。
senses.why: When a person rather than a text is described, the sense becomes a habitual pursuit.
senses.whyCN: 当描述对象从文本换成人物时，词义变成一种惯常的追逐。

senses.title: Relating to the emotion of love in general
senses.definition: of the feelings of attachment and affection between people
senses.definitionCN: 泛指人与人之间的依恋与爱慕之情
senses.example: Her letters reveal an amatory turmoil of youth.
senses.exampleCN: 她的信件透露出年轻时情感上的纷乱。
senses.why: Beyond physical desire, the word can name the whole emotional state of loving.
senses.whyCN: 超出肉体欲望之外，这个词也能指称恋爱情感的整个状态。

intro.en: Amatory comes from Latin amor (love), the root that also gives amateur and amorous.
intro.cn: amatory 源自拉丁语 amor（爱），与 amateur、amorous 同根。

items.en: A root meaning to love or desire, generally reconstructed as *am-.
items.cn: 一般认为源自表示「爱、欲」的重构词根 *am-。

items.en: amor, "love", and amatorius, "of a lover, loving".
items.cn: 拉丁语 amor「爱」；amatorius「恋人的；钟情的」。

items.en: amatorius used by classical authors for love poetry and lovers.
items.cn: 古典作家用 amatorius 形容情诗与恋人。

items.en: English amatory appears in the sixteenth century in learned writing.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语 amatory 出现于学术性书面语。

items.en: Now a literary word for anything concerning love, especially in formal description.
items.cn: 如今是书面语词，指一切与爱情有关的事物，尤用于正式描述。

note.en: Distinguish amatory from its root family amor/amateur/amorous and from look-alike am- words.
note.cn: 要把 amatory 与词族 amor/amateur/amorous 区分开，也要与形近的 am- 开头词区分。

entries.definition: same Latin root, but stressing being in love or showing desire.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，更强调「坠入爱河、流露情欲」的状态。

entries.definition: same root: one who does something for the love of it, a non-professional.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词：因喜爱而做某事的人，即非职业爱好者。

entries.definition: a different Latin word sharing only the am- spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 另一个拉丁语词，只是拼写开头相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: relating to love with an idealized, imaginative coloring.
entries.definitionCN: 指带有理想化、浪漫想象色彩的爱情。

entries.definition: more explicit term for sexual desire or arousal.
entries.definitionCN: 更直接指性欲与情欲的词。

entries.definition: full of strong feeling, not only of the romantic kind.
entries.definitionCN: 充满强烈情感的，不限于爱情。

normalIntro.en: Remember amatory through its Latin root of love.
normalIntro.cn: 通过拉丁语词根「爱」记住 amatory。

normal.en: amor (love) + -atory (of): of love.
normal.cn: amor（爱）+ -atory（与……有关）：爱情的。

normal.en: Same root as amorous and amateur: all grew from love.
normal.cn: 与 amorous、amateur 同根：都源自「爱」。

normal.en: An amateur works for love of it; amatory works are about love.
normal.cn: amateur 为爱而做；amatory 写的正是爱。

normal.en: Think of Cupid, the little god of amor.
normal.cn: 想想丘比特——掌管 amor 的小爱神。

normal.en: It is a bookish word: amatory verse, amatory fiction, amatory adventures.
normal.cn: 它是书面语词：常见于 amatory verse、amatory fiction、amatory adventures。

abstract.en: Picture a quill pen dipping into red ink to write a love poem.
abstract.cn: 想象一支鹅毛笔蘸着红墨水写情诗。

abstract.en: See Cupid drawing his bow over a stack of love letters.
abstract.cn: 看丘比特在一摞情书上方张弓搭箭。

abstract.en: Feel the hush of a candlelit room where a sonnet is read aloud.
abstract.cn: 感受烛光房间里有人轻声朗读情诗的静谧。

examples.en: The anthology collects amatory poetry from six centuries.
examples.cn: 这部选集收录了六个世纪的爱情诗。

examples.en: Their amatory correspondence was discovered years later.
examples.cn: 多年后他们的情书往来被发现。

examples.en: Critics regard it as a landmark of amatory fiction.
examples.cn: 评论界视其为言情小说的里程碑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿玛托丽」——阿玛托丽姑娘人人爱，她的名字写满了情书。

root: 拉丁语 amor（爱，一般认为源自重构词根 *am-「爱、欲」）派生形容词 amatorius（恋爱的），进入英语后为 amatory，字面义为「属于爱的」。同族词有 amorous（多情的）、amateur（爱好者）。

sensesIntro.en: From love poetry, the senses extend to desire, loving behavior, the romance genre, and a life of courtship.
sensesIntro.cn: 从爱情诗出发，义项扩展到情欲、示爱行为、言情体裁与风流生涯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pen devoted only to writing about love
core.cn: 核心意象：一支专为爱情而动的笔

branches.en: Love and courtship in general, as in love poetry.
branches.cn: 泛指爱情与求爱，如情诗。

branches.en: Physical desire and the whole emotional state of loving.
branches.cn: 肉体情欲与恋爱情感的整体状态。

branches.en: The manner typical of a lover.
branches.cn: 恋人特有的举止神态。

branches.en: The literary genre built on romantic plots.
branches.cn: 以恋爱情节为主线的文学体裁。

branches.en: A life given to romantic adventures.
branches.cn: 醉心恋爱韵事的生涯。

intro.en: Amatory is a Latin love root with a learned adjective suffix.
intro.cn: amatory 由拉丁语「爱」词根加学术性形容词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The root amor passed directly from Latin into learned English vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 amor 直接从拉丁语进入英语学术词汇。

items.meaning: one who, of the nature of
items.exampleCN: 见拉丁语 amatorius、英语 amatory

latinEntries.example: amor vincit omnia in Latin verse
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁诗句 amor vincit omnia（爱征服一切）
古典拉丁语中的 carmina amatoria（情诗）

definition_zh: adj./adv. 两月一次的（地）；每月两次的（地）；n. 双月刊
definition_en: happening every two months, or twice a month; a publication issued on such a schedule
core_image: 日历上两个月才被圈中一格的约会，和一个月里被圈中两格的约会
scene: 这本杂志是双月刊，每两个月出一期。 The magazine is bimonthly, so a new issue appears every two months.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bimonthly 可指每两个月一次的；句意是这本杂志为双月刊，两个月出一期。

pos.zh: 两月一次的；一月两次的

forms.label: 形容词与副词原级（无屈折变化）

derivatives.zh: 两周一次的；一周两次的

senses.title: Every two months
senses.definition: appearing or happening once every two months
senses.definitionCN: 每两个月出现或发生一次
senses.example: The journal is bimonthly, with six issues a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这份期刊是双月刊，一年六期。
senses.why: Bi- can be read as every, and month supplies the interval, so the word can mean once in two months.
senses.whyCN: bi- 可理解为「每隔」，加 month 表间隔，故可指两个月一次。

senses.title: Twice a month
senses.definition: appearing or happening two times in each month
senses.definitionCN: 每月出现或发生两次
senses.example: Some clinics hold bimonthly checks, one at the start and one mid-month.
senses.exampleCN: 有些诊所每月查两次，月初一次、月中一次。
senses.why: The same prefix also carries the sense of twice, so the word is famously ambiguous.
senses.whyCN: 同一个前缀也含「两次」之义，因此这个词以歧义著称。

intro.en: Bimonthly is Latin bi- joined to the English word month and the ending -ly.
intro.cn: bimonthly 是拉丁语 bi- 接英语 month，再加词尾 -ly。

items.en: Bis means twice, and its combining form is bi-.
items.cn: bis 意为两次，其构词形式为 bi-。

items.en: Old English monath is the month, named for the moon.
items.cn: 古英语 monath 即月份，因月亮而得名。

items.en: The compound bimonth appears in periodical writing.
items.cn: 复合词 bimonth 出现在期刊文字中。

items.en: Bimonthly is coined for publications and meetings.
items.cn: bimonthly 为出版物与会议而造。

items.en: Editors complain that readers cannot tell which sense is meant.
items.cn: 编辑抱怨读者分不清是哪一种含义。

items.en: Many style guides advise every two months in plain phrasing.
items.cn: 现代写作指南建议直接写成「每两个月」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bi- or -ly shape; the near-meaning group runs through the schedule words from twice a month to once a year.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bi- 或 -ly 的形状；近义组按频率从每月两次排到每年一次。

entries.definition: Every two weeks or twice a week.
entries.definitionCN: 两周一次或一周两次的。

entries.definition: Happening twice each year.
entries.definitionCN: 一年两次的。

entries.definition: Happening twice each year.
entries.definitionCN: 一年两次的。

entries.definition: Twice each month.
entries.definitionCN: 每月两次的。

entries.definition: Happening once each month.
entries.definitionCN: 每月一次的。

entries.definition: Happening once every three months.
entries.definitionCN: 每季度一次的。

entries.definition: Happening once each year.
entries.definitionCN: 每年一次的。

entries.definition: Repeating at set intervals.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定间隔重复的。

normalIntro.en: Bi- is the ambiguous piece: it can mean twice or every two, so bimonthly covers both schedules.
normalIntro.cn: bi- 是那个含糊的部分：既可指「两次」，也可指「每隔两个」，所以 bimonthly 两种日程都管。

normal.en: Bi- plus month plus -ly, three pieces only.
normal.cn: bi- 加 month 加 -ly，只有三块。

normal.en: With two months, it is six issues a year.
normal.cn: 按两个月算，一年六期。

normal.en: With twice a month, it is twenty-four issues a year.
normal.cn: 按每月两次算，一年二十四期。

normal.en: When in doubt, spell the schedule out in words.
normal.cn: 拿不准时，干脆用文字把频率写清楚。

normal.en: Compare biannual, which has the same double reading.
normal.cn: 可比 biannual，它同样有两种读法。

abstract.en: A calendar with only two circles on it.
abstract.cn: 日历上只画了两个圈。

abstract.en: A clock with a missing hand.
abstract.cn: 缺了一根指针的钟。

abstract.en: A word that refuses to give one date.
abstract.cn: 一个不肯给出单一日期的词。

examples.en: The board meets bimonthly, in March, May and so on.
examples.cn: 董事会每两个月开一次会，三月、五月依此类推。

examples.en: Her column appears bimonthly in a science magazine.
examples.cn: 她的专栏在一份科学杂志上每两月刊出一次。

examples.en: Ask the clinic whether bimonthly here means twice a month.
examples.cn: 问问诊所这里的 bimonthly 是不是指每月两次。

dict_mnemonic.text: bi 是「二」，month 是「月」——两个月一次，也可能是一个月两次，所以看到这个词一定要问清楚。

root: 拉丁 bi-（二；每两）+ 古英语 monath（月）+ -ly（形容词、副词词尾）

sensesIntro.en: The two senses are not an accident but the prefix itself: bi- can count occurrences or count the interval.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项并非偶然，而是前缀本身：bi- 既可数次数，也可数间隔。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one calendar with two circles far apart and another with two circles close together
core.cn: 核心意象：一张日历上两个相隔很远的圈，另一张上两个挨得很近的圈

branches.en: An issue arriving in spring and then in summer.
branches.cn: 春季来一期，夏季再来一期。

branches.en: A review meeting every other month.
branches.cn: 隔月一次的评审会。

branches.en: A check on the first and the fifteenth.
branches.cn: 一日与十五日各查一次。

branches.en: Two paydays in one month.
branches.cn: 一个月里的两个发薪日。

branches.en: A frequency that must be asked about.
branches.cn: 必须追问清楚的频率。

intro.en: Bimonthly stacks a Latin numeral, an English time word and a suffix; the list below builds the whole family of frequency words.
intro.cn: bimonthly 由一个拉丁数词、一个英语时间词和一个词尾叠成；下面列出整族频率词。

latinIntro.en: Latin bis is twice, mensis is a month, and annus is a year.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 bis 意为两次，mensis 意为月，annus 意为年。

items.exampleCN: 每月两次的；半年一次的

latinEntries.example: Mensis lies behind menstrual and semester.
latinEntries.exampleCN: mensis 是 menstrual 与 semester 的来源。
annus 产生 annual 与 anniversary。

definition_zh: 暂时无效；中止；搁置
definition_en: a state of temporary inactivity or suspension
core_image: 钟摆停在最边上的位置，等着下一次推动
scene: 新楼规划公示已挂半年，邻里都在等消息。 The building plan has been in abeyance since the funding fell through.
sceneCN: 这里 abeyance 是「中止、搁置」（第 1 个义项：暂时停摆的状态）；句意为自资金落空后，建楼计划一直处于搁置状态。

pos.zh: 暂时无效；中止；搁置（状态）

derivatives.zh: 由名词加 -ant 构成，义为「中止的；暂时无效的」
法律短语名词，义为「暂缓条款」

senses.title: Temporary suspension of activity
senses.definition: a state in which something expected or ongoing is stopped for a while
senses.definitionCN: 预期进行之事被暂停一段时间的状态
senses.example: Negotiations were held in abeyance until the elections ended.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判被搁置，直到选举结束。
senses.why: Old French abeance meant a gazing or longing toward something; the matter stands looking at its goal without moving.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 abeance 意为「对某事张望渴求」；事情就那样望着目标而不动。

senses.title: Undetermined ownership or title
senses.definition: a legal state in which a right, title, or succession is not settled
senses.definitionCN: 权利、所有权或继承尚未确定的法律状态
senses.example: The barony fell into abeyance among several heirs.
senses.exampleCN: 男爵爵位在数位继承人之间处于悬置状态。
senses.why: When no one can hold the right, the law lets it stand open like a chair no one sits in.
senses.whyCN: 当无人能持有时，法律让它像一把无人落座的椅子般空着。

senses.title: A lapsed custom
senses.definition: a custom or practice that has gradually stopped being observed
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐停止被遵行的惯例
senses.example: The old ceremony fell into abeyance two generations ago.
senses.exampleCN: 那项古老仪式两代人以前便不再举行。
senses.why: What once moved regularly can slow until it stands still; the word names that standing still.
senses.whyCN: 曾经规律运行的事物会慢下来直至停摆；这个词命名的就是这种停摆。

intro.en: Abeyance descends from Old French abeance, a gazing or expectancy, built on a verb meaning to gape at.
intro.cn: abeyance 源自古法语 abeance「张望、期待」，其动词意为「对……张口凝视」。

items.en: A Frankish root for gaping is reconstructed behind the French verb, related to abash's source.
items.cn: 法语动词背后重构出一个法兰克语「张口」词根，与 abash 的来源相关。

items.en: Abeer meant to gape at or aspire; abeance was the state of longing attention.
items.cn: 古法语 abeer 意为凝望、渴求；abeance 指渴慕注视的状态。

items.en: Abeyance entered English law for ownership waiting to settle.
items.cn: 盎格鲁-法语 abeyance 进入英国法律，指待定的所有权。

items.en: The word widened to any temporary stop.
items.cn: 十六世纪起该词扩大为一切暂时中止。

items.en: In abeyance remains the standard phrase for suspension.
items.cn: in abeyance 至今仍是表示中止的标准短语。

note.en: Abeyance keeps company with other suspension words and shares an old root with abash.
note.cn: abeyance 与其他「中止」类词同群，并与 abash 共享一个古老的词根。

entries.definition: to embarrass, from the same gaping root
entries.definitionCN: 使窘迫；与 abeyance 同出「张口」词根

entries.definition: adjective meaning suspended
entries.definitionCN: 形容词形式，义为中止的

entries.definition: a temporary stopping
entries.definitionCN: 暂停；语域更通用

entries.definition: an official delay or halt
entries.definitionCN: 正式的延期或冻结；多为官方决定

entries.definition: an uncertain waiting state
entries.definitionCN: 悬而不决的状态；口语色彩更强

normalIntro.en: Five anchors tie abeyance to the paused clock.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手把 abeyance 与停摆的钟绑在一起。

normal.en: in abeyance is the phrase to memorise.
normal.cn: 要背的短语是 in abeyance。

normal.en: Picture a pendulum stopped mid-swing.
normal.cn: 想象钟摆停在半摆的位置。

normal.en: Lawyers use it for unsettled titles.
normal.cn: 律师用它表示权属未定。

normal.en: fall into abeyance: a custom quietly dying.
normal.cn: fall into abeyance：惯例悄悄废止。

normal.en: It shares its gaping root with abash.
normal.cn: 它与 abash 共享「张口」词根。

abstract.en: Hear music stop between two bars.
abstract.cn: 听见乐声在两小节之间停住。

abstract.en: See a revolving door frozen halfway.
abstract.cn: 看见旋转门冻在半途。

abstract.en: Feel the pause where a decision should be.
abstract.cn: 感到本该有决定之处的停顿。

examples.en: The rule remained in abeyance until the board met again.
examples.cn: 在董事会再次开会之前，该规则一直搁置未行。

examples.en: Traffic fines were held in abeyance during the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水期间交通罚款暂停执行。

examples.en: The title fell into abeyance when the last baron died without a son.
examples.cn: 末代男爵无子而终，爵位遂陷入悬置。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「鹅被摁住」——鹅被摁住动弹不得，只好暂停一切

root: 古法语 abeance「凝望渴求」＝ a-（拉丁 ex- 之转）＋ beance「张口」（日耳曼语源，与 abash 同词根，词根属重构形式）。经盎格鲁-法语进入英国法律，再扩大为一般「中止」义。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses hold one pose: standing still before a goal, whether law, plan, or custom.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项保持同一姿态：在目标前静止，无论是法律、计划还是惯例。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pendulum frozen at the edge of its swing.
core.cn: 核心意象：钟摆冻在摆动的边缘。

branches.en: THE PAUSED PLAN: activity stops but may resume.
branches.cn: 暂停的计划：活动停止但可恢复。

branches.en: THE OPEN SEAT: a right waits with no holder.
branches.cn: 空着的座位：权利等待持有者。

branches.en: THE SLEEPING CUSTOM: practice that quietly stopped.
branches.cn: 沉睡的惯例：悄悄停止的实践。

branches.en: TIME HOLDS STILL: both senses are pauses that stretch.
branches.cn: 时间静止：这两个义项都是延长的暂停。

branches.en: ONE STANDING STILL: every sense is motion withheld, not ended.
branches.cn: 同一种静止：每个义项都是被搁置而非终止的运动。

intro.en: A French prefix and a Germanic root meet in one noun ending.
intro.cn: 法语前缀与日耳曼词根在一个名词词尾中会合。

latinIntro.en: Only the prefix a- goes back to Latin ex-; the gaping root is Germanic and reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 只有前缀 a- 可回溯到拉丁语 ex-；「张口」词根属日耳曼语重构形式。

items.example: It aims the verb at an object.
It turns the verb into abeyance.
It shares the same gaping root.
items.exampleCN: 它与本词同享「张口」词根。

items.example: It is thought to hold the same Germanic element.
items.exampleCN: 一般认为它含同一日耳曼成分。

items.example: It is the verb behind the noun.

derivatives.zh: 由名词加 -ant 构成，义为「中止的」

definition_zh: 官僚机构；官僚体制；繁文缛节；（任何大型组织的）层级管理层
definition_en: the system of officials and offices that runs public business through ranks, files and fixed rules
core_image: 一排挂着编号的窗口，表格在窗口之间来回传递，每个窗口只负责盖一个章
scene: 办事的人被从一个窗口送到下一个窗口，手里那叠表格始终少一个章。 The bureaucracy moved her file through six windows before anyone read it.
sceneCN: 这里 bureaucracy 指按层级与规章运转的行政机构（第 1 个义项：作为机构整体）；句意为这套官僚机构把她的档案过了六个窗口，才有人真正读它。

pos.zh: 官僚机构；官僚体制（可数，指一套机构；不可数，指这种运作方式）
繁文缛节；官僚作风（口语中带贬义）

derivatives.zh: 官僚（bureau + -crat「掌权者」，由机构转指机构中的人）
官僚的；程序繁琐的（bureaucrat + -ic，由人转指其作风）
使官僚化（bureaucrat + -ize，由名词转指使之变成那样的过程）
官僚化（bureaucratize + -ation，由动作转指该过程及其结果）

senses.title: The administrative apparatus
senses.definition: the whole body of offices and officials that carries out public business
senses.definitionCN: 执行公共事务的整套机关与人员
senses.example: The bureaucracy grew faster than the services it delivered.
senses.exampleCN: 这套行政机构的扩张快于它所提供的服务。
senses.why: the -cracy ending names a form of rule, so the word first denotes a governing apparatus rather than one clerk.
senses.whyCN: -cracy 这一后缀指某种统治形式，因此这个词首先指治理机关，而非某一位办事员。

senses.title: Officials as a body
senses.definition: the class or corps of career officials, seen as sharing interests and habits
senses.definitionCN: 职业官员构成的群体，被视为共享利益与习惯
senses.example: The reform was resisted by the bureaucracy itself.
senses.exampleCN: 改革遭到官僚群体本身的抵制。
senses.why: once offices became careers, the people in them could be spoken of as a single body with its own outlook.
senses.whyCN: 一旦职位成为职业，任职者便可被当作一个有自身心态的整体来谈论。

senses.title: Red tape
senses.definition: the forms, stamps and waiting that a procedure imposes before anything can be done
senses.definitionCN: 办事之前必须经历的表格、盖章与等待
senses.example: Bureaucracy delayed the permit by eleven weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 繁文缛节让许可证晚了十一周。
senses.why: the everyday sense is a metonymy: the apparatus is named by the annoyance it produces.
senses.whyCN: 日常义是转喻：用机构造成的麻烦来指称机构本身。

senses.title: Hierarchy in any large body
senses.titleCN: 任何大型组织的层级管理
senses.definition: the managerial layer of a university, hospital or company, with ranks, files and approval chains
senses.definitionCN: 大学、医院或公司中的管理层，带等级、档案与审批链
senses.example: Every large hospital has a bureaucracy of its own.
senses.exampleCN: 每一所大医院都有自己的官僚层。
senses.why: Weber's analysis showed the pattern is not peculiar to states, so the word spread to any large organization.
senses.whyCN: 韦伯的分析表明这种模式并非国家独有，于是这个词扩展到一切大型组织。

senses.title: Rule by files, not by persons
senses.definition: administration in which written rules and records, not personal ties, decide outcomes
senses.definitionCN: 由成文规则与档案、而非私人关系来决定结果的行政方式
senses.example: Rule by files, not by persons, was the point of the reform.
senses.exampleCN: 按规章而非人情办事，正是这场改革的要点。
senses.why: the defining feature is impersonality: the same rule must bind the clerk and the petitioner alike.
senses.whyCN: 其要点是非人格化：同一条规则对办事员与申请者一视同仁。

senses.title: Weber's ideal type
senses.definition: a neutral analytic model of administration by hierarchy, written records, trained staff and fixed jurisdiction
senses.definitionCN: 一种中性的分析模型：层级、文书、受训人员与固定职权范围
senses.example: Weber's ideal type describes bureaucracy without praising it.
senses.exampleCN: 韦伯的理想型只是描述官僚制，并不赞美它。
senses.why: the sociological sense strips the word of insult and turns it into a set of testable features.
senses.whyCN: 社会学义剥去贬义，把它变成一组可检验的特征。

senses.title: Sluggishness blamed on rules
senses.definition: the pejorative reading: delay, evasion and rigidity produced by too many rules
senses.definitionCN: 贬义读法：规则过多造成的拖延、推诿与僵化
senses.example: The licence stalled for months in what officials called bureaucratic inertia.
senses.exampleCN: 官僚惰性这一说法正好描述了这个贬义读法。
senses.why: the same features that make administration predictable also make it slow, so the word carries both judgements.
senses.whyCN: 使行政可预期的那套特征同时也让它迟缓，因此这个词兼带两种评价。

senses.title: Size and cost of the apparatus
senses.titleCN: 机构膨胀带来的规模与成本
senses.definition: the sheer scale of an administrative machine and what it costs to keep running
senses.definitionCN: 行政机器本身的庞大规模，以及维持它运转的开销
senses.example: Auditors measured the bureaucracy by headcount and floor space.
senses.exampleCN: 审计人员用人数与办公面积来衡量这套机构。
senses.why: budgets make the apparatus visible as a quantity, and that quantity is what the word names here.
senses.whyCN: 预算把机关显形为一个数量，这里命名的正是那个数量。

intro.en: Bureaucracy is a French coinage of the early nineteenth century: bureau 'desk, office' plus -cratie 'rule', from Greek kratos 'power'. It began as a satirical label. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: bureaucracy 是 19 世纪初的法语新造词：bureau「书桌、办公室」加 -cratie「统治」，后者来自希腊 kratos「力量」。它最初是讽刺性标签。年代均为约数。

items.en: Bureau first meant a coarse woollen cloth used to cover writing desks, then the desk itself, then the room and the office.
items.cn: bureau 最初指铺在写字桌上的粗毛布，继而指桌子本身，再指房间与机关。

items.en: Kratos meant 'strength, might', and the -kratia suffix named a form of rule, as in democracy and aristocracy.
items.cn: kratos 意为「力量、强权」，-kratia 后缀表示某种统治形式，如 democracy 与 aristocracy。

items.en: Bureaucratie was coined in French around the 1810s as a mocking term for government carried on by officials rather than by citizens.
items.cn: bureaucratie 于 1810 年代前后在法语中造出，用来讥讽由官员而非公民运转的政府。

items.en: English adopted bureaucracy in the nineteenth century; Mill used it for the corps of officials, a usage that made the word descriptive rather than merely hostile.
items.cn: 英语在 19 世纪借用该词；密尔用它指官员群体，这一用法使词从纯敌意转为描述性。

items.en: Weber turned bureaucracy into a technical term for administration by hierarchy, written records, trained staff and fixed jurisdiction.
items.cn: 韦伯把官僚制转为术语，指以层级、文书、受训人员与固定职权范围进行的行政。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the origin of burel, the cloth behind bureau, is not established, and the pre-Greek origin of kratos is unsettled, so any older form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深来源）：bureau 背后的 burel 那种布料的来源未得到证明；kratos 在希腊语之前的来源亦无定论，凡为其提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one shares the -cracy or bureau stock; group two holds words for administration and its annoyances.
note.cn: 第一组共享 -cracy 或 bureau 词干；第二组是行政及其麻烦的同近义词。

entries.definition: A single official, formed with -crat 'one who holds power'; the longer word names the system, not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个官员，由 -crat「掌权者」构成；较长的词指整套制度，而非个人。

entries.definition: The adjective describing procedure-heavy behaviour; it modifies a noun instead of naming the apparatus.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述程序繁多的作风；它修饰名词，而不指称机关。

entries.definition: Aristos 'best' plus kratos: rule by a supposed elite. It shares the suffix but not the desk.
entries.definitionCN: aristos「最优者」加 kratos：由所谓精英统治。后缀相同，词根无关。

entries.definition: Autos 'self' plus kratos: rule by one person with unrestricted power, a contrast to rule by offices.
entries.definitionCN: autos「自身」加 kratos：一人不受限制地统治，与由机关统治相对。

entries.definition: The activity of managing an organization, neutral in tone; bureaucracy adds the sense of ranks and procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 管理组织的活动，语气中性；bureaucracy 另带层级与程序之意。

entries.definition: The permanent employees of the state, named by their employment rather than by their procedures.
entries.definitionCN: 国家的常任雇员，按雇佣关系命名，而非按程序命名。

entries.definition: The delays and forms only, with no reference to the offices that produce them.
entries.definitionCN: 只指拖延与表格，不涉及产生它们的机关。

entries.definition: Officials thought of as a class with shared habits, close to the second sense of bureaucracy.
entries.definitionCN: 被视为共享习气的官员阶层，接近 bureaucracy 的第二义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: bureau 'desk' + -cracy 'rule': rule carried out from desks.
normal.cn: bureau「书桌」+ -cracy「统治」：从书桌后面实施的统治。

normal.en: The family runs bureaucrat, bureaucratic, bureaucratize, bureaucratization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 bureaucrat、bureaucratic、bureaucratize、bureaucratization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the complaint: cut bureaucracy, layers of bureaucracy, red tape.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出抱怨的语气：精简官僚程序、层层官僚机构、繁文缛节。

normal.en: The same suffix appears in democracy, aristocracy and autocracy, all through Greek kratos.
normal.cn: 同一后缀出现在 democracy、aristocracy、autocracy，都经希腊 kratos。

normal.en: Weber's four marks: hierarchy, written files, trained staff, fixed jurisdiction.
normal.cn: 韦伯的四项标志：层级、文书档案、受训人员、固定职权。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase where every step requires a signature before the next step opens.
abstract.cn: 想象一道楼梯，每上一级都要先签一个字，下一级才打开。

abstract.en: Picture a machine that works perfectly and produces only paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一台运转完美的机器，产出只有纸。

abstract.en: Picture a queue in which nobody knows who is first, but everyone holds a numbered slip.
abstract.cn: 想象一条队列，没人知道谁在前，但人人手里都有一张编号纸条。

examples.en: The new agency added a layer of bureaucracy without adding a service.
examples.cn: 新机构加了一层官僚机构，却没增加一项服务。

examples.en: Small firms complain that bureaucracy eats their first month.
examples.cn: 小公司抱怨官僚程序吃掉了它们头一个月。

examples.en: Weber saw bureaucracy as the most efficient form of large-scale administration.
examples.cn: 韦伯认为官僚制是大规模行政中最有效率的形式。

dict_mnemonic.text: bureau（办公桌）+ cracy（统治）＝ 靠一张张办公桌和一个个章运转的统治；记「章多、层多、纸多」。

root: 法语 bureaucratie = bureau「书桌、办公室」（源自 burel 粗毛布，其来源不确定）+ -cratie「统治」（希腊 kratos「力量」，希腊语之前的来源属重构形式）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one object seen from different distances: the whole apparatus, the people inside it, the paper it produces, the same pattern in any large body, its impersonality, its analytic model, its slowness, and its cost.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项是对同一对象的远近不同取景：整套机关、其中的群体、它产出的纸、任何大型组织里的同一模式、它的非人格化、它的分析模型、它的迟缓、它的成本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a corridor of numbered windows where a file gains one stamp per window and never quite finishes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条挂编号窗口的走廊，档案每过一个窗口多一个章，却始终办不完。

branches.en: MACHINE AND MEN: first the offices, then the career officials who staff them.
branches.cn: 机器与人：先看机关，再看在其中任职的官员。

branches.en: THE SAME FEATURE READ TWICE: forms make work predictable and also make it slow.
branches.cn: 同一特征的两读：表格让工作可预期，也让工作变慢。

branches.en: THE SHAPE TRAVELS: hospitals and firms reproduce the state's pattern.
branches.cn: 形状在迁移：医院与公司复制了国家的模式。

branches.en: NEUTRAL CORE: rule by files, then the model that states it without blame.
branches.cn: 中性内核：先是按档案办事，再是把它不带褒贬地陈述出来的模型。

branches.en: COUNTED: budgets turn the apparatus into headcount and floor space.
branches.cn: 被计数：预算把机关变成人数与面积。

intro.en: Bureaucracy is a French compound whose two parts still work separately in English: bureau for the office, -cracy for a form of rule.
intro.cn: bureaucracy 是法语复合词，两部分在英语中仍各自运作：bureau 指机关，-cracy 指某种统治形式。

latinIntro.en: The second element goes back to Greek kratos through the suffix -kratia; the first element is French and has no Latin source.
latinIntro.cn: 第二部分经后缀 -kratia 上溯希腊 kratos；第一部分属法语，没有拉丁来源。

items.example: The bureau keeps the land records.

items.meaning: a form of rule or dominance
items.example: Democracy and autocracy share this suffix.
items.exampleCN: 民主制与专制共享这一后缀。

items.meaning: a member or supporter of a ruling group
items.meaningCN: 某一统治群体的成员或支持者
items.exampleCN: 技术官僚凭专业知识治理。

items.example: The bureaucrat stamped the form without reading it.
items.exampleCN: 那位官员没看就盖了章。

items.example: Bureaucratic delays cost the project a season.
items.exampleCN: 官僚拖延让项目耽误了一季。
他们把志愿网络官僚化了。
合并之后便出现了官僚化。

items.meaning: the inflated style of official writing
items.example: The notice was written in bureaucratese.
items.exampleCN: 这则通知是用公文腔写的。

definition_zh: 艺术史；艺术史学科；（某一时期或地区的）艺术发展史
definition_en: the academic study of the history and development of the visual arts, or the history of art in a particular period or place
core_image: 一排按年代挂起的画，被一条关于风格、赞助与观看方式的线索穿起来
scene: 讲堂的屏幕上，两幅相隔百年的画被并排放置，学生被要求找出构图的变化。 The lecture used two paintings a century apart to show how art history compares styles.
sceneCN: 这里 art history 指「作为学科的艺术史」（第 1 个义项：系统研究艺术发展及其方法的学问）；句意为这堂课用相隔一个世纪的两幅画，说明艺术史如何比较风格。

pos.zh: 艺术史；艺术史学科（通常不可数，特定叙述时可数）

forms.label: 可数用法（少见，指多种叙述）

derivatives.zh: art history + -an（从业者）→ 艺术史学者；从「学科」转到「研究该学科的人」
art history + -al（关系形容词）→ 艺术史的；从「领域」转到「属性」
history + -ic（关系形容词）→ 有历史意义的；从「记录」转到「值得记录」
historic + -ally（副词后缀）→ 在历史上；从「性质」转到「观察角度」
history + -an（人）→ 历史学家；从「叙述」转到「写叙述的人」

senses.title: The academic discipline
senses.definition: the scholarly study of art and its development, with its own methods and questions
senses.definitionCN: 对艺术及其发展进行学术研究，并形成自身方法与问题的学科
senses.example: She studied art history in Florence.
senses.exampleCN: 她在佛罗伦萨学习艺术史。
senses.why: The compound joins a subject (art) to a method of inquiry (history), so the name denotes the discipline that applies historical questions to works of art.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把对象「艺术」与探究方式「历史」连接起来，因此命名的是把历史问题用于艺术作品的学科。

senses.title: A course or programme
senses.definition: a class or programme in this field
senses.definitionCN: 该领域的一门课程或培养项目
senses.example: Art history is a required course for the major.
senses.exampleCN: 艺术史是这个专业的必修课。
senses.why: A discipline taught becomes a course, so the same name can denote the slot in a timetable rather than the whole field.
senses.whyCN: 被教授的一门学科会成为课程，因此同一个名称也能指课表上的一个位置，而不是整个领域。

senses.title: The actual development of art
senses.definition: the history of art as it happened, independent of how it is studied
senses.definitionCN: 艺术实际发生的历史，不依赖人们如何研究它
senses.example: The art history of the period is one of rapid experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 这一时期的艺术史充满快速实验。
senses.why: History can mean the events themselves, not only the study of them; the compound inherits both readings from its second element.
senses.whyCN: history 既可指事件本身，也可指对事件的研究；复合词从第二个成分继承了这两种读法。

senses.title: A particular written account
senses.titleCN: 关于艺术发展的一种叙述
senses.definition: a book or account that narrates the development of art
senses.definitionCN: 叙述艺术发展的一部书或一种说法
senses.example: His book offers a new art history of the interwar years.
senses.exampleCN: 他的书提供了两次大战之间年代的一种新艺术史叙述。
senses.why: Every history is also a telling, so the compound can name one narrative among rivals rather than the objective sequence.
senses.whyCN: 每一种历史也是一种叙述，因此复合词能指与竞争叙述并列的一种讲法，而不是客观序列。

senses.title: Art history of a place or period
senses.titleCN: 某地或某时期的艺术史
senses.definition: the history of art in a specified region, period or tradition
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区、时期或传统中的艺术史
senses.example: The art history of Venice is inseparable from its trade.
senses.exampleCN: 威尼斯的艺术史与它的贸易密不可分。
senses.why: Restricting the compound with of or a place-name turns the whole discipline into a bounded subject: this art history, here.
senses.whyCN: 用 of 或地名限定这个复合词，就把整门学科变成一个有限对象：此地的这一段艺术史。

senses.title: The scholarly literature
senses.definition: the body of published research on a work, artist or question
senses.definitionCN: 关于某件作品、某位艺术家或某个问题的已发表研究总体
senses.example: The art history on this workshop fills three shelves.
senses.exampleCN: 关于这个工坊的艺术史研究文献装满了三层书架。
senses.why: The discipline is also the sum of what has been written; the uncountable use shifts from activity to accumulated text.
senses.whyCN: 学科也是已写成之物总和；不可数用法从「活动」转到「累积的文本」。

senses.title: A method of visual analysis
senses.definition: a method of analysing works through their forms, materials and visual structure
senses.definitionCN: 通过形式、材料与视觉结构分析作品的方法
senses.example: Formal art history begins with a close reading of the surface.
senses.exampleCN: 形式分析的艺术史从对画面的细读开始。
senses.why: Because the discipline developed distinct techniques, its name can stand for the technique itself, especially when contrasted with theory or criticism.
senses.whyCN: 由于这门学科发展出多种技术，其名称也可指技术本身，尤其在与理论或批评对照时。

senses.title: A department or scholarly community
senses.definition: the institutional unit or community of scholars working in the field
senses.definitionCN: 从事该领域工作的院系单位或学者群体
senses.example: The art history department shares a building with the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 艺术史系与博物馆共用一栋楼。
senses.why: Metonymy turns the subject into the people and rooms that teach it: the department is called by the name of its field.
senses.whyCN: 转喻把学科变成教授它的人与房间：院系用其领域的名称来称呼。

intro.en: Art history joins two old words, Latin ars and Greek historia, into a modern compound; the discipline took shape in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: art history 把两个古老的词——拉丁 ars 与希腊 historia——合成一个现代复合词；这门学科在 19 世纪成形。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ars, artis meant practical skill, a craft, or a system of rules; the modern category of fine art grew out of this word.
items.cn: ars、artis 意为实用技艺、手艺或规则体系；现代「美术」这一类别就是从这个词生长出来的。

items.en: Greek historia meant 'inquiry, learning by investigation, a written account'; it came from histōr 'witness, judge'.
items.cn: 希腊 historia 意为「探究、通过调查获得的知识、书面叙述」，来自 histōr「见证者、评判者」。

items.en: Latin borrowed historia as a narrative of events; Old French histoire and Middle English history carried it into English.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 historia，指对事件的叙述；古法语 histoire 与中古英语 history 把它带入英语。

items.en: Art history is a modern English compound: the object plus the inquiry. Similar compounds such as natural history and church history were already established.
items.cn: art history 是现代英语复合词：对象加探究方式。natural history、church history 等类似复合词此前已经确立。

items.en: Universities, museums and printed catalogues turned the study of art's past into a taught discipline with chairs, journals and methods.
items.cn: 大学、博物馆与印刷图录把对艺术过去的研究变成有教席、期刊与方法的可授学科。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): no single first citation for the compound is agreed, and the boundary between antiquarian description and art history is itself debated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个复合词没有公认的最早书证，而且古物描述与艺术史之间的界线本身也有争议。

note.en: Group one holds the academic labels most often swapped with art history; group two holds neighbouring ways of studying art that ask different questions.
note.cn: 第一组是最常与 art history 混用的学科名称；第二组是研究艺术但问题不同的邻近路径。

entries.definition: The scholar who works in the field; art history is the field itself.
entries.definitionCN: 在该领域工作的学者；art history 是领域本身。

entries.definition: The evaluation of works, usually present-tense; art history reconstructs their place in time.
entries.definitionCN: 对作品的评价，通常是当下时态；艺术史则重建作品在时间中的位置。

entries.definition: The conceptual framework for understanding art; it need not follow dates or provenance.
entries.definitionCN: 理解艺术的概念框架；不必按年代或来源展开。

entries.definition: General instruction in how to look at and enjoy art, usually without original research.
entries.definitionCN: 教人如何观看与欣赏艺术的通识课程，通常不含原创研究。

entries.definition: The study of all visual media, including advertising and scientific images; art history keeps the fine-art core.
entries.definitionCN: 研究一切视觉媒介，包括广告与科学图像；艺术史保留美术核心。

entries.definition: The study of museums, collecting and display; it uses art history but focuses on institutions.
entries.definitionCN: 研究博物馆、收藏与展示；会使用艺术史，但焦点在机构。

entries.definition: The expert judgement of authorship, date and quality; a handmaid to art history rather than the whole discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 对作者、年代与品质的专家判断；是艺术史的辅助技艺，而非整门学科。

entries.definition: The history of beliefs and practices, of which art may be one source; art history keeps works at the centre.
entries.definitionCN: 信念与实践的历史，艺术只是其中一种材料；艺术史把作品放在中心。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: art + history: the history of art, then the discipline that writes it.
normal.cn: art + history：艺术的历史，然后是书写这段历史的学科。

normal.en: history goes back to Greek historia 'inquiry'; the discipline is an inquiry, not a list of dates.
normal.cn: history 上溯希腊 historia「探究」；这门学科是探究，不是年表。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: art history department, art history survey, a degree in art history.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：艺术史系、艺术史通史课、艺术史学位。

normal.en: The family runs art, history, historian, art historian and art historical.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 art、history、historian、art historian 与 art historical。

normal.en: A museum label often gives the 'art historical' date, while the wall text gives the criticism.
normal.cn: 博物馆标签常给出「艺术史」年代，墙面说明则给出评论。

abstract.en: Picture paintings hung in a row, each one turning to face the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一排挂起的画，每幅都转过来面对下一幅。

abstract.en: Picture a timeline drawn through a gallery rather than along a page.
abstract.cn: 想象一条时间线穿过画廊，而不是画在纸页上。

abstract.en: Picture a question mark placed over a finished masterpiece.
abstract.cn: 想象一个问号落在一件已完成的杰作上。

examples.en: Art history asks not only what a work looks like but who paid for it.
examples.cn: 艺术史不只问作品长什么样，还问是谁出钱做的。

examples.en: The department teaches art history alongside conservation and museum studies.
examples.cn: 该系把艺术史与修复、博物馆研究放在一起教授。

examples.en: Her art history of the region begins with a single church door.
examples.cn: 她写的该地区艺术史从一扇教堂门开始。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「art（艺术）+ history（历史）」——给艺术写的历史 → 艺术史

root: art 来自拉丁 ars（属格 artis）「技艺」；history 来自希腊 historia「探究、叙述」，经拉丁 historia 与古法语 histoire。二者合成现代英语复合词 art history，19 世纪成为学科。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses separate the discipline from its course, its actual past, its narratives, its literature, its method and its institutional home.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把学科与课程、实际过去、叙述、文献、方法及机构归属分开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of paintings is threaded by one line about style, patronage and the way viewers looked.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排画被一条关于风格、赞助与观看方式的线索穿起来。

branches.en: THE FIELD AND ITS HOME: the discipline as knowledge, then the department that teaches it.
branches.cn: 学科及其归属：先作为知识的学科，再是教授它的院系。

branches.en: THE COURSE: the discipline cut down to a timetable slot.
branches.cn: 课程：学科被切成课表上的一个位置。

branches.en: WHAT HAPPENED: the events themselves, before any account is written.
branches.cn: 实际发生：在任何叙述写成之前的事件本身。

branches.en: ACCOUNTS, LITERATURE AND METHOD: one telling, the accumulated shelf of tellings, and the trained way of reading form.
branches.cn: 叙述、文献与方法：一种讲法，累积成架的各种讲法，以及阅读形式的训练有素的方法。

branches.en: A BOUNDED SUBJECT: the whole discipline restricted to one place or period.
branches.cn: 有限对象：整门学科被限定到一地或一时。

intro.en: The phrase is a transparent compound of a Latin-derived noun and a Greek-derived noun, so both halves can be read with their own histories.
intro.cn: 这个短语是拉丁来源名词与希腊来源名词的透明复合词，两半都能连同自身历史一起读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies ars for the first half and historia, borrowed from Greek, for the second; historia itself comes from Greek histōr 'witness'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语为前半提供 ars，为后半提供借自希腊语的 historia；historia 本身来自希腊 histōr「见证者」。

items.exampleCN: art 命名被研究的对象。

items.meaning: an inquiry into the past; a narrative

items.example: Art history began to be taught in universities.
items.exampleCN: 艺术史开始在大学里被教授。

items.meaning: a person connected with a field
items.exampleCN: historian 用的是同一个词尾。

items.example: The art historian dated the panel by its frame.
items.exampleCN: 这位艺术史学者通过画框为木板画定年。

items.example: The question is art historical, not chemical.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题属于艺术史，而不是化学。

items.meaningCN: 历史上有重要意义的；有记载的
items.example: The sale was a historic event for the museum.
items.exampleCN: 这次收购对博物馆是历史性事件。

items.meaning: relating to the past as recorded
items.meaningCN: 与有记载的过去有关的

latinEntries.meaning: inquiry; a written account of events
latinEntries.meaningCN: 探究；对事件的书面叙述

latinEntries.meaning: a craftsman; a maker by skill

definition_zh: 指称；声称；（未经证实地）断言；援引作为理由
definition_en: to state that something is true or that someone did something wrong, without proof
core_image: 一个人在文件页脚签下「据称」，把未核实的事推到桌面上
scene: 调查员把一份手写材料放进档案袋，说明材料里提到的细节还没有核实。 The complaint alleges that the landlord ignored repeated repair requests.
sceneCN: 这里 allege 指提出尚未证实的说法（第 1 个义项：断言某事为真而尚未举证）；句意为投诉材料称房东无视了多次维修请求。图中可辨识物件：投诉表、档案袋、手写便条、签字笔。

pos.zh: 指称；声称；（未经证实地）断言
（法律）援引、引证作为理由或依据

senses.title: State something as true
senses.titleCN: 指称某事为真，尚未举证
senses.definition: to state that something is the case without offering proof
senses.definitionCN: 断言某事确实如此，但未提供证据
senses.example: The complaint alleges that the landlord ignored repeated repair requests.
senses.exampleCN: 投诉材料称房东无视了多次维修请求。
senses.why: Latin allegare meant 'to bring forward, adduce'; a claim is brought forward before the proof that would support it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 allegare 意为「提出、援引」；说法先被提出，支持它的证据后才可能到来。

senses.title: State it in a pleading
senses.titleCN: 在诉状或正式文书中陈述
senses.definition: to set out a fact as true in a legal or official document
senses.definitionCN: 在法律或官方文书中把某项事实陈述为真
senses.example: The plaintiff alleges that the contract was signed under duress.
senses.exampleCN: 原告主张合同是在胁迫下签署的。
senses.why: In pleadings the verb marks a fact the party undertakes to prove, so the legal sense keeps its forward-looking force.
senses.whyCN: 在诉状中，这个动词标出一项当事人承诺日后证明的事实，因此法律义保留了「向前提出」的劲头。

senses.title: Name a person's act
senses.definition: to say that a named person performed a particular act
senses.definitionCN: 指认某个具体的人做过某件具体的事
senses.example: The article alleges that two officials took payments from the contractor.
senses.exampleCN: 文章指称两名官员收受了承包商的款项。
senses.why: The pattern allege that someone did something lets a newspaper name the act while leaving the proof to others.
senses.whyCN: 「指称某人做过某事」这一结构让报纸点明行为，同时把举证留给别人。

senses.title: Cite as a reason
senses.definition: to offer something as a reason, excuse or justification
senses.definitionCN: 把某事物作为理由、借口或正当依据提出
senses.example: He alleged pressure from his superiors as the reason for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 他称上级施加的压力是延误的原因。
senses.why: Adducing a reason is literally bringing something forward, so the same verb serves for excuses and justifications.
senses.whyCN: 提供理由字面上就是把某物提出来，因此同一个动词也能用于借口与辩解。

senses.title: Cite a precedent or text
senses.definition: to quote a case, a rule or a passage in support of an argument
senses.definitionCN: 为支持论点而援引案例、规则或文句
senses.example: Counsel alleged two earlier rulings in support of the claim.
senses.exampleCN: 律师援引了先前两份裁决来支持这一主张。
senses.why: A precedent is also brought forward into an argument, and the old sense of adducing survives in this usage.
senses.whyCN: 先例同样是被提出来放进论证，于是「援引」的旧义在这一用法中留存。

senses.title: Plead in excuse
senses.definition: to plead something as an excuse, an older sense now largely confined to legal and literary texts
senses.definitionCN: 把某事当作辩解提出，这一旧义如今多限于法律与文学文本
senses.example: In the old account he alleged illness and left the assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧时的记述里，他称病离开了集会。
senses.why: The older sense of adducing a defence survives in legal phrasing, where a party alleges facts to escape liability.
senses.whyCN: 「提出抗辩」的旧义残留在法律措辞里：一方援引事实以摆脱责任。

senses.title: The alleged offender
senses.titleCN: 分词形容词：被指称的，涉嫌的
senses.definition: alleged, as an adjective: named in a claim but not proved guilty
senses.definitionCN: alleged 作形容词：被指称但尚未证实有罪的
senses.example: The alleged offender was never charged.
senses.exampleCN: 被指称的涉案人从未被起诉。
senses.why: The past participle marks a person named in a claim but not yet tried, which is exactly the gap the verb describes.
senses.whyCN: 过去分词标记「被指称却尚未受审」的人，正好对应这个动词所描述的缺口。

senses.title: The reported claim
senses.titleCN: 被动与副词形式：据称、据悉
senses.definition: be alleged to and allegedly: forms that report a claim while keeping the speaker at a distance
senses.definitionCN: 这类转述形式把说法归到他人名下，同时让说话者保持距离
senses.example: The firm is alleged to have moved the money offshore.
senses.exampleCN: 据称该公司把钱转移到了海外。
senses.why: Reported forms are the safest way for a paper to repeat a charge it cannot prove.
senses.whyCN: 对无法举证的指控，转述形式是报纸最稳妥的表达方式。

intro.en: Allege comes through Anglo-French aleger from Latin allegare 'to send forward, adduce', built on ad- 'to' and legare 'to send, depute'. It entered English in the fourteenth century as a pleading verb. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: allege 经盎格鲁—法语 aleger 来自拉丁 allegare「向前送出、援引」，由 ad-「朝向」与 legare「派出、委派」构成，十四世纪作为诉讼用语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Legare meant 'to send as a deputy' and also 'to bequeath'; the root has no connection with law.
items.cn: legare 意为「作为代表派出」，也有「遗赠」义；这个词根与「法律」无关。

items.en: Ad- plus legare gave allegare 'to bring forward, adduce, plead as evidence'.
items.cn: ad- 加 legare 构成 allegare「向前提出、援引、作为证据陈说」。

items.en: Anglo-French aleger carried the legal verb into English courts in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 盎格鲁—法语 aleger 在十四世纪把这个法律动词带入英格兰的法庭。

items.en: In pleading, to allege was to state a fact that the party undertook to prove later.
items.cn: 在诉讼中，allege 指陈述一项当事人承诺日后加以证明的事实。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the verb was used outside court for any claim put forward without proof, and the passive became the reporter's default.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个动词在法庭之外用于任何未经证实而提出的说法，被动式则成了报道的默认写法。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the tie between legare and the root of legere 'to gather, choose' is generally thought but not proved; first records are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：一般认为 legare 与 legere「收集、挑选」的词根有关，但未获证实；最早书证为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words that share letters or a look with allege but not its root; group two holds verbs of asserting, ranked by how much proof they imply.
note.cn: 第一组是字母或外形与 allege 相近、却不同源的词；第二组是断言类动词，按所含证据分量排列。

entries.definition: From ligare 'to bind', so it means loyalty owed, not a claim made.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 ligare「捆绑」，指所负的忠诚，而不是提出的说法。

entries.definition: From legare 'bequeath': what a will or a past age leaves behind.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 legare「遗赠」：遗嘱或过往时代留下的东西。

entries.definition: From legare 'send as a deputy': an official envoy, especially a papal one.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 legare「作为代表派出」：官方使节，尤指教廷使节。

entries.definition: From Greek allegoria 'speaking otherwise'; a story carrying a second meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 allegoria「换个说法」：承载第二层含义的故事。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for saying something is true, with no suggestion that proof is missing.
entries.definitionCN: 说某事为真的日常动词，不暗示缺少证据。

entries.definition: To state something confidently; it stresses the speaker's conviction rather than the lack of proof.
entries.definitionCN: 自信地陈述某事，强调说话者的确信，而非缺少证据。

entries.definition: To say someone did wrong; it always targets a person or body, while allege often targets a fact.
entries.definitionCN: 指某人做错事，总有一个被指对象；而 allege 常指向一件事实。

entries.definition: To argue that something is true as part of a dispute, implying opposing views.
entries.definitionCN: 在争论中主张某事为真，暗示存在对立观点。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Ad- 'to' plus legare 'send': a claim sent forward for others to test.
normal.cn: ad-「朝向」加 legare「送」：把说法送到别人面前去检验。

normal.en: The family runs allege, allegation, alleged, allegedly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 allege、allegation、alleged 与 allegedly。

normal.en: News prose prefers the passive: the company is alleged to have...
normal.cn: 新闻语体偏爱被动式：据称该公司曾……

normal.en: A pleading alleges facts; the other side then admits or denies them.
normal.cn: 诉状提出事实主张，随后由对方承认或否认。

normal.en: Allegiance is a false friend from the binding root, not from sending.
normal.cn: allegiance 是假朋友，来自「捆绑」的词根，与「送出」无关。

abstract.en: Picture a claim pushed through a door before anyone checks who is behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个说法被推进门里，却没人先确认门后是谁。

abstract.en: Picture a signature at the foot of a page that nobody has read to the end.
abstract.cn: 想象一页没人读完的文件，页脚已经有了签名。

abstract.en: Picture a label reading reported stuck to a parcel nobody has opened.
abstract.cn: 想象一只贴着「据报」标签、却没人拆开过的包裹。

examples.en: The study alleges a link between the two chemicals and the illness.
examples.cn: 这项研究称这两种化学品与那种疾病存在关联。

examples.en: It was alleged that the files had been destroyed before the hearing.
examples.cn: 据称档案在听证之前就已被销毁。

examples.en: She alleged no reason for the delay and simply left.
examples.cn: 她没有给出延误的任何理由，就此离开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「a + lege（送出）」——话先送出去，证据后再补：指称、声称

root: 拉丁 allegare「向前提出、援引」= ad-（朝向）+ legare「派出、送出」；英语 allege 经盎格鲁—法语 aleger 进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses trace one move: a claim is sent forward, then the settings change from court to newspaper to quotation, and finally to the grammatical forms that report it at arm's length.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个动作展开：说法先被送出去，接着场景从法庭换到报纸再到引证，最后落在把那项说法隔开距离转述的语法形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone signs the word reported at the foot of a page and pushes the unverified sheet across the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：有人在页脚签下「据称」，把未核实的纸推到桌子对面。

branches.en: THE CLAIM SENT: the same move serves a newspaper sentence and a formal pleading.
branches.cn: 送出的说法：同一个动作既用于报纸句子，也用于正式诉状。

branches.en: THE ACT NAMED: a person and a deed are specified, while the proof stays elsewhere.
branches.cn: 点明的行为：指出具体的人与具体的事，证据却留在别处。

branches.en: THE REASON ADDUCED: a pressure, a precedent or a passage is brought forward in support.
branches.cn: 援引的理由：把压力、先例或文句提出来充当依据。

branches.en: THE OLD DEFENCE: pleading illness or some other fact to escape a duty belongs to an older legal idiom.
branches.cn: 古老的辩解：称病或以其他事实脱责，属于更早的法律习语。

branches.en: THE REPORTED FORM: the participle and the adverb let a writer repeat a charge without owning it.
branches.cn: 转述形式：分词与副词让写作者重复一项指控，却不必替它担保。

intro.en: Allege is a Latin verb whose prefix, root and suffixes each build other English words.
intro.cn: allege 是一个拉丁动词，前缀、词根与后缀各自还构成别的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin legare gives legate, legacy and legation; allege and allegation come from allegare, where ad- adds direction. Allegiance belongs to the binding root and not here.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 legare 衍生 legate、legacy 与 legation；allege 与 allegation 出自 allegare，由 ad- 增添方向义。allegiance 属于「捆绑」词根，不在这一族。

items.example: The prefix pushes the claim into view.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把说法推到人前。
这个词根提供「送出」的意思。

items.meaning: to bring forward as a claim
items.example: The report alleges that the forms were altered.
items.exampleCN: 报告指称这些表格被改动过。

items.example: The alleged theft was never reported.
items.exampleCN: 被指称的盗窃从未有人报案。

items.example: The clerk allegedly deleted the file.

items.example: The legate carried a sealed letter.
items.exampleCN: 使节带着一封密封的信。

definition_zh: v. 使丢脸；使不可信；怀疑　n. 不信；怀疑；名誉丧失
definition_en: to harm the reputation of someone or make something seem untrue; loss of respect or belief
core_image: 一张证书上的印章被人用黑笔涂掉；法庭上证人的话被一条红线划去
scene: 那篇报道意在抹黑这位科学家。 The report was meant to discredit the scientist.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：报道的目的就是让这位科学家的话不再被人相信。

senses.title: Damage a reputation
senses.definition: to make people stop respecting or trusting someone
senses.definitionCN: （动词）让人不再尊重或信任某人
senses.example: The report was meant to discredit the scientist.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇报道意在抹黑这位科学家。
senses.why: A certificate with its seal crossed out in black ink.
senses.whyCN: 一张证书上的印章被黑笔涂掉。

senses.title: Show to be untrue
senses.definition: to make an idea or claim seem false or unreliable
senses.definitionCN: （动词）让某个说法显得虚假或不可靠
senses.example: New evidence discredited the old theory.
senses.exampleCN: 新证据推翻了旧理论。
senses.why: A witness statement with a red line through it.
senses.whyCN: 一份证词被红线划去。

senses.title: Loss of belief or respect
senses.definition: the state of no longer being believed or respected
senses.definitionCN: （名词）不再被相信或尊重的状态
senses.example: The scandal brought discredit on the whole firm.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻让整家公司蒙羞。
senses.why: A nameplate pried off an office door.
senses.whyCN: 一块从办公室门上撬下来的名牌。

intro.en: Discredit is dis- plus credit; credit goes back through Italian credito to Latin creditum, a thing entrusted, from credere, to believe.
intro.cn: discredit 由 dis-（去掉）加 credit（信任、信用）构成；credit 经意大利语 credito 上溯拉丁语 creditum「被托付之物」，来自 credere「相信」。

items.en: Latin credere means to believe or entrust.
items.cn: 拉丁语 credere 意为相信、托付。

items.en: Creditum meant a thing entrusted or a loan.
items.cn: creditum 意为被托付之物或借款。

items.en: Italian credito carried the sense of belief and trust.
items.cn: 意大利语 credito 带有相信与信任的意思。

items.en: Credit entered English for belief and for money lent.
items.cn: credit 进入英语，表示相信，也表示借出的钱。

items.en: Dis- was added to give discredit, to take belief away.
items.cn: 加上 dis- 得到 discredit，意为把信任拿走。

items.en: The noun sense of lost reputation follows the verb.
items.cn: 表示名誉丧失的名词义随动词而来。

note.en: Discredit is credit with belief removed; its neighbours share the believe root or mean attacking trust.
note.cn: discredit 是把信任拿走的 credit；它的邻居要么同「相信」词根，要么表示攻击信任。

entries.definition: belief, trust, or money lent; also praise earned
entries.definitionCN: 相信、信任或借出的钱；也指获得的赞誉

entries.definition: able to be believed or trusted

entries.definition: the quality of being believable

entries.definition: to show that a claim or idea is wrong

entries.definition: to weaken something gradually, often secretly

entries.definition: to damage the reputation of a person by false statements
